definition_zh: 联赛；联盟；同盟；（旧）结盟
definition_en: a group of sports teams that compete against one another, an alliance of states or groups, and an older verb meaning to unite in such an alliance
core_image: 一排球队队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗之间用绳子系在一起
scene: 赛季开始前，球迷在球场外排起长队。Their team finished top of the league last season.
sceneCN: 这里 league 指「联赛」（第 1 个义项）；句意为他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。图中可辨识物件：队旗、球场看台、积分榜。

derivatives.zh: 由 league 与 table 复合，指联赛积分榜
由 non- 加 league 构成，指不属于职业联赛的
league 的复数形式，也可指很远的距离，如 leagues away

senses.title: A group of teams competing against each other
senses.definition: an organized group of sports clubs or teams that play against one another for a title
senses.definitionCN: 为争夺冠军而相互比赛的有组织的体育俱乐部或队伍
senses.example: Their team finished top of the league last season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。
senses.why: A league was first a group bound by an agreement, and teams bound into a fixture list are exactly that: a set of rivals tied to the same schedule.
senses.whyCN: league 最初指由协议绑在一起的一群人，而被赛程绑在一起的球队正是如此：一群被同一张日程拴住的对手。

senses.title: An alliance of states or groups
senses.definition: an association of countries, parties or groups formed to act together
senses.definitionCN: 为共同行动而组成的国家、政党或团体联合体
senses.example: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。
senses.why: Latin ligare means to bind, so the political sense is the literal one: separate parties tied by a treaty into one body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以政治义才是字面义：彼此独立的各方被条约绑成一个整体。

senses.title: To unite in an alliance
senses.definition: to join together with others in an alliance, now mainly literary or historical
senses.definitionCN: 与他人联合结成同盟，现在多用于文学或历史叙述
senses.example: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。
senses.why: If a league is a body bound together, then to league is simply to enter that binding, which is why the verb mirrors the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果 league 是被绑在一起的整体，那么 to league 就是加入这次捆绑，因此动词与名词完全对应。

intro.en: League comes from a Latin verb meaning to bind, by way of Italian and French, so an alliance is literally a tying together.
intro.cn: league 经意大利语和法语来自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词，所以同盟字面上就是「绑在一起」。

items.en: Ligare meant to bind or tie, and a league was first a binding together of people.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、结合，而 league 最初指把人们绑在一起。

items.en: Italian lega named an alliance, a group bound by an agreement.
items.cn: 意大利语 lega 指同盟，即由协议绑在一起的一群人。

items.en: Old French ligue carried the political sense of a confederacy into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ligue 把「邦联、同盟」这一政治含义带进英语。

items.en: Middle English league named an alliance of rulers, and by the sixteenth century it also named a group of sports sides.
items.cn: 中古英语 league 指统治者之间的同盟，到十六世纪也指一组体育队伍。

items.en: Modern English keeps the alliance sense in phrases such as in league with, while the sports sense dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语在 in league with 等说法中保留同盟义，体育运动义则主导日常使用。

note.cn: 形近组收 league 的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示同盟的词。

normalIntro.en: The word means a binding, and both a treaty and a fixture list are ways of tying separate parties into one arrangement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「捆绑」，而条约与赛程都是把彼此独立的一方绑进同一安排的方式。

normal.en: Latin ligare means to bind, so a league is people or teams tied together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以 league 就是被绑在一起的人或球队。

normal.en: The League of Nations was literally a binding of states after a war.
normal.cn: 国际联盟字面上就是战后各国的一次捆绑。

normal.en: In league with somebody usually hints at a secret or dishonest binding.
normal.cn: in league with somebody 通常暗示一种秘密或不正当的勾结。

normal.en: A football league is a binding by schedule: every club must play every other.
normal.cn: 足球联赛是一种按赛程的捆绑：每个俱乐部都必须与其他俱乐部比赛。

normal.en: To league is the old verb for entering that alliance, now mostly literary.
normal.cn: to league 是表示加入同盟的旧动词，现在多用于文学。

abstract.en: Competition and alliance share one word because both require parties to accept the same set of obligations.
abstract.cn: 竞争与同盟共用一个词，因为两者都要求各方接受同一套义务。

abstract.en: A league is a promise made visible: the table, the fixture list, the treaty are its rope.
abstract.cn: 联赛是把承诺变得可见：积分榜、赛程、条约就是它的绳子。

abstract.en: To be in league is to be tied to someone, whether by trust or by guilt.
abstract.cn: 身处一个 league 就是与某人绑在一起，不论靠信任还是靠罪责。

definition_zh: 倾斜；倚靠；倾向；瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的
definition_en: to bend or rest against something, to tend towards a view, or to be thin, without fat or spare resources
core_image: 一个人把肩膀靠向窗框，身子斜成一条线
scene: 雨夜的车站里，旅人把肩膀靠向窗边的墙，望着外面的水汽。She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「倚靠、倾斜」（第 2 个义项：把身体靠在某物上）；句意为她靠着窗看雨。可辨识画面：车站、窗边的旅人、玻璃上的水汽。

pos.zh: 瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的

derivatives.zh: 由 lean 加 -ing 构成，义为「倾向；倾斜」
由 lean 加 -ly 构成，义为「精瘦地」
由 lean 加 -ness 构成，义为「瘦；贫乏」
由 lean 与 to 复合，义为「单坡棚屋」

senses.title: To bend away from upright
senses.definition: to slope or bend away from a vertical position
senses.definitionCN: 偏离垂直位置而倾斜
senses.example: The old fence leans to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 那道旧篱笆向左倾斜。
senses.why: Old English hleonian meant to bend or recline, and the body's tilt is the picture the word starts from.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hleonian 意为弯下、躺靠，身体倾斜的样子就是这个词起笔的画面。

senses.title: To rest against something
senses.definition: to put your weight on something while standing or sitting
senses.definitionCN: 站或坐时把重量放在某物上
senses.example: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠着窗看雨。
senses.why: If a body bends sideways, it must be held up by something, so the tilt becomes support.
senses.whyCN: 身体若向一侧弯，就得有别的东西撑住，倾斜于是变成依靠。

senses.title: To tend towards an opinion
senses.definition: to favour one choice or view more than another
senses.definitionCN: 更支持某一种选择或看法
senses.example: The committee leans towards a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。
senses.why: Mind leaning to one side mirrors a body leaning on a wall, so the same verb covers opinions.
senses.whyCN: 心思靠在一边，正如身体靠在墙上，同一个动词便也用来指看法。

senses.title: Thin, without much fat
senses.definition: thin in a healthy way, with little fat and firm muscle
senses.definitionCN: 瘦得健康，脂肪少而肌肉结实
senses.example: The runner had a lean, strong build.
senses.exampleCN: 那名跑步者体格精瘦有力。
senses.why: A separate Old English adjective hlǣne meant thin, and English merged it into the same spelling as the verb.
senses.whyCN: 另有一个古英语形容词 hlǣne 意为瘦，英语把它并入了与动词相同的拼写。

senses.title: Meat with little fat
senses.definition: meat that contains little fat
senses.definitionCN: 含脂肪很少的肉
senses.example: She bought lean beef for the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。
senses.why: Thinness applied to meat simply means the fat has been left out, an easy extension of the bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 「瘦」用在肉上只表示去掉了脂肪，是身体义的自然延伸。

senses.title: Short of money or supplies
senses.definition: limited in money or resources, as in lean years
senses.definitionCN: 钱财或资源有限，如艰难的年头
senses.example: The company survived several lean years.
senses.exampleCN: 公司熬过了好几个艰难的年头。
senses.why: A body without fat has nothing to spare, and a budget in the same state is called lean.
senses.whyCN: 身上没脂肪就没有余量，处于同样状态的预算也被称为 lean。

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, were pulled into one spelling in English.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，在英语里被拉进了同一个拼写。

items.en: Hleonian meant to lean, bend or recline, and it is the source of the verb.
items.cn: hleonian 意为倾、弯、躺靠，是动词的来源。

items.en: A separate adjective hlǣne meant lean or thin, with no fat to spare.
items.cn: 另有一个形容词 hlǣne，意为瘦、没有多余脂肪。

items.en: Middle English lenen kept the verb, and the adjective was pulled into the same spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语 lenen 保留了动词，形容词也被拉进同一拼写。

items.en: The two words met in form, so one spelling now carries both bending and thinness.
items.cn: 两个词在形式上相遇，于是一个拼写同时承载「倾斜」与「瘦」。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to meat, budgets and hard years.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词义扩展到肉、预算与艰难的年头。

note.cn: 形近组收这个词的各种形式以及只差一个字母的词；近义组收表示瘦与倾斜的词。

entries.definition: A small shelter with a sloping roof against a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 靠墙搭起、屋顶倾斜的小棚。

entries.definition: In a thin, spare way.
entries.definitionCN: 以精瘦、简省的方式。

entries.definition: A legal claim on property until a debt is paid.
entries.definitionCN: 债务清偿前对财产的法定扣押权；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To jump a long way or suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 长距离或突然地跳。

entries.definition: Having little fat or width.
entries.definitionCN: 脂肪或厚度小的。

entries.definition: Thin in an attractive or graceful way.
entries.definitionCN: 纤细而好看的。

entries.definition: Thin, often used of a deliberate or healthy figure.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦的，常指刻意保持或健康的体形。

entries.definition: To slope or lean to one side.
entries.definitionCN: 向一侧倾斜。

normalIntro.en: A verb of bending and an adjective of thinness share one spelling, so every sense sits between a tilted body and a body with no spare fat.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词共用一个拼写，所以每个义项都落在「倾斜的身体」与「没有多余脂肪的身体」之间。

normal.en: Hleonian is the Old English verb for leaning, and it is the ancestor of the body sense.
normal.cn: hleonian 是古英语里表示倚靠的动词，是身体义的祖先。

normal.en: Hlǣne was a different Old English adjective for thin, so the adjective lean and the verb lean started apart.
normal.cn: hlǣne 是另一个古英语形容词，意为瘦，所以形容词 lean 与动词 lean 起初并不相干。

normal.en: Lean on and lean towards keep the picture of weight moved onto something or someone.
normal.cn: lean on 与 lean towards 保留了「把重量移到某物或某人身上」的画面。

normal.en: Lean meat is meat with the fat cut away, not meat that tilts.
normal.cn: lean meat 是去掉脂肪的肉，不是会倾斜的肉。

normal.en: Lean years are years with nothing to spare, the body sense turned into a budget.
normal.cn: lean years 是没有余量的年头，把身体义转成了预算。

abstract.en: One spelling holds two histories, so context decides whether lean is about a body or about a shortage.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写装着两段历史，所以语境决定 lean 说的是身体还是短缺。

abstract.en: Leaning on something is trust made visible: weight is handed over.
abstract.cn: 靠住某物是看得见的信任：重量被交了出去。

abstract.en: Fat is spare capacity, so a lean body and a lean budget both mean there is no margin.
abstract.cn: 脂肪是余量，所以精瘦的身体与紧缩的预算都意味着没有余地。

examples.en: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
examples.cn: 她靠着窗看雨。

examples.en: The committee leans towards a later start.
examples.cn: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。

examples.en: She bought lean beef for the soup.
examples.cn: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离嗯」——身体离开竖直，靠向一边，嘴里还「嗯」了一声；记住 lean 是倾斜、倚靠。

root: 动词来自古英语 hleonian（倾靠），形容词来自古英语 hlǣne（瘦），两词在现代英语中拼写合一。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body tilted onto support; the senses then add opinions, a thin body, lean meat and a lean budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一具斜靠在支撑物上的身体；义项由此加上看法、瘦削的身体、瘦肉与紧缩的预算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoulder pressed to a window frame, the body a straight line at an angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩膀抵着窗框，身体斜成一条直线。

branches.en: an old fence slowly going sideways
branches.cn: 慢慢歪向一边的旧篱笆

branches.en: a traveller's shoulder against a rainy window
branches.cn: 旅人的肩靠在下雨的窗上

branches.en: a committee raising hands for one option
branches.cn: 委员会为某个选项举手

branches.en: a runner with firm muscle and no spare fat
branches.cn: 肌肉结实、没有多余脂肪的跑者

branches.en: an empty account book in a hard year
branches.cn: 艰难年头里空空的账本

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, plus English endings, make up this word.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，再加上英语词尾，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: Both the verb and the adjective are Old English, and no Latin cognate is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 动词与形容词都来自古英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 学习；学会；得知；记住；背诵
definition_en: to gain knowledge or a skill, to become aware of a fact, and to commit something to memory
core_image: 一个孩子用手指着书上的字母，一个音一个音地把它们连起来
scene: 教室里很安静，只有翻书的声音。Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
sceneCN: 这里 learn 指「学习、学会」（第 1 个义项）；句意为孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。图中可辨识物件：课本、字母表、孩子的指读手势。

derivatives.zh: 由 learn 加 -er 构成，指学习者
由 learn 加 -ing 构成，指学习、学识
由 learn 加 -able 构成，指可学会的

senses.title: To gain knowledge or a skill
senses.definition: to come to know something or to be able to do something through study or practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习或练习而知道某事或会做某事
senses.example: Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。
senses.why: The Old English verb named the act of acquiring knowledge, and its noun lār, teaching or lore, shows that learning was always something passed from one person to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词指获取知识的行为，它的名词 lār（教导、学问）说明「学」始终是从一个人传到另一个人的事。

senses.title: To become aware of a fact
senses.definition: to be told about something or to discover a piece of information
senses.definitionCN: 被告知某事或发现某条信息
senses.example: We learned of the delay only this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们直到今天早上才得知延期的消息。
senses.why: Knowledge does not have to be studied: hearing a piece of news also fills the gap, so the verb extends from lessons to any newly acquired fact.
senses.whyCN: 知识不一定来自苦读：听到一条消息同样能补上空白，于是词义从课堂扩展到任何新获得的事实。

senses.title: To commit something to memory
senses.definition: to fix words or facts in the memory so that they can be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 把词句或事实记在脑中，以便复述
senses.example: The class learned the poem by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把这首诗背了下来。
senses.why: Ancient learning often meant memorizing texts aloud, so the verb kept a narrower sense of storing words in the head for later recitation.
senses.whyCN: 古代的学习常意味着出声背诵文本，因此这个词保留了「把词句存进脑中以便日后复述」的窄义。

intro.en: Learn is an Old English verb of the Germanic family, and its related noun survives in the modern word lore.
intro.cn: learn 是日耳曼语族的古英语动词，它的相关名词保存在现代英语 lore 一词中。

items.en: Leornian meant to acquire knowledge, and its noun lār, teaching or lore, survives in the word lore.
items.cn: leornian 意为获取知识，其名词 lār（教导、学问）保存在 lore 一词中。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family of learning words; a link to a root meaning to track or follow a furrow is often suggested but not certain.
items.cn: 这个动词属于日耳曼语的学习词族；常有人提出它与「跟踪、沿犁沟走」的词根有关，但并不确定。

items.en: Middle English lernen kept both to learn and, in some regions, to teach, a double use that lasted for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语 lernen 既指学，也在部分地区指教，这种两用持续了几个世纪。

items.en: The past forms learned and learnt competed, and the irregular learnt held on in British usage.
items.cn: 过去式 learned 与 learnt 竞争，不规则的 learnt 在英式用法中留存下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps learn for gaining knowledge or news, while the old teach sense survives only in dialect and in nonstandard speech.
items.cn: 现代英语的 learn 指获取知识或得知消息，古老的「教」义只在方言与非标准口语中留存。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and derivatives of learn; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for acquiring knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组收 learn 的形式与派生词；近义组收其他表示获取知识的动词。

entries.definition: A person who is learning something.
entries.definitionCN: 正在学习某事的人。

entries.definition: Knowledge gained through study, or the process of gaining it.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习获得的知识，或获取它的过程。

entries.definition: The British irregular past form of learn.
entries.definitionCN: learn 的英式不规则过去式。

entries.definition: To spend time reading and thinking about a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 花时间阅读并思考某个学科。

entries.definition: To fix something in the memory deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把某物记在脑中。

entries.definition: To gain a skill or possession over time.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐获得技能或财物。

entries.definition: To find out something that was not known before.
entries.definitionCN: 发现此前不知道的事情。

normalIntro.en: The word names the act of gaining knowledge, and it has kept a plain, practical tone since Old English.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指获取知识的行为，自中古英语以来一直保持着朴素、实用的语气。

normal.en: Old English leornian meant to gain knowledge, and its noun lār is the ancestor of lore.
normal.cn: 古英语 leornian 意为获取知识，其名词 lār 是 lore 的前身。

normal.en: Learner and learning simply add -er for the person and -ing for the activity.
normal.cn: learner 与 learning 只是分别加 -er 表示人、加 -ing 表示活动。

normal.en: Learn by heart keeps the memory sense, because the words are stored inside rather than looked up.
normal.cn: learn by heart 保留记忆义，因为词句是被存进脑中而非查出来的。

normal.en: Learn of the delay uses the news sense: knowledge arriving without study.
normal.cn: learn of the delay 用的是「得知」义：知识未经苦读就到来了。

normal.en: British English allows both learned and learnt, while American English prefers learned.
normal.cn: 英式英语过去式 learned 与 learnt 都可用，美式英语则更常用 learned。

abstract.en: A word for learning once also meant teaching, because the same knowledge moves between two people in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 表示「学」的词曾经也指「教」，因为同一份知识在两个人之间反向流动。

abstract.en: Learning is not only reading: a rumour, a mistake and a poem all leave something behind.
abstract.cn: 学习不只是读书：一则传闻、一次错误、一首诗都会留下点什么。

abstract.en: What is learned by heart is carried without a book, which is why memory was once the main library.
abstract.cn: 背下来的东西不用书也能带着走，这就是记忆曾是主要图书馆的原因。

examples.en: Children learn to read by sounding out each letter.
examples.cn: 孩子们通过把每个字母读出声来学会阅读。

examples.en: We learned of the delay only this morning.
examples.cn: 我们直到今天早上才得知延期的消息。

examples.en: The class learned the poem by heart.
examples.cn: 全班把这首诗背了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐恩」——把学习当成一件乐事、一份恩赐；谐音记住 learn 是学习、得知。

root: 古英语 leornian（学习、获取知识），属日耳曼语词族；相关名词 lār 演变为今天的 lore（学问）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is gaining knowledge; it widens to hearing news and narrows again to memorizing words for recitation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是获得知识；它扩展到听到消息，又收窄为把词句背下来以便复述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child pointing at letters and joining their sounds one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子指着字母，把一个个音连起来。

branches.en: a child sounding out a first word
branches.cn: 孩子把第一个词读出声

branches.en: an apprentice watching a craftsman's hands
branches.cn: 学徒看着匠人的手

branches.en: a phone call bringing unexpected news
branches.cn: 一个电话带来意外的消息

branches.en: a poem repeated until it is fixed in the head
branches.cn: 反复念到记牢的一首诗

branches.en: a class reciting together without a book
branches.cn: 全班不看书齐声背诵

intro.en: The word is a bare Old English verb, and English builds its family with -er, -ing and -able while keeping a Germanic irregular past.
intro.cn: 这个词是光秃秃的古英语动词，英语用 -er、-ing 与 -able 扩展词族，同时保留日耳曼语的不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for learn; the verb and its noun belong to the Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: learn 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，这个动词及其名词都属日耳曼语族。

definition_zh: 皮革；皮革制品；皮制的
definition_en: material made from the skin of animals, articles made from it, or the material used before a noun
core_image: 一块鞣好的牛皮摊在木台上，边缘还留着刀痕
scene: 作坊里，匠人把一张厚皮按在木台上，用刀顺着边裁下。The smell of new leather filled the small workshop.
sceneCN: 这里是「皮革」（第 1 个义项：动物皮制成的材料）；句意为新皮革的气味充满这间小作坊。可辨识画面：木台、厚皮、裁皮刀。

derivatives.zh: 由 leather 加 -y 构成，义为「像皮革的；坚韧的」
由 leather 加 -ette（仿制品）构成，义为「人造革」
由 leather 加 -en（由……制成的）构成，义为「皮革制的」（古旧用法）
由 leather 与 back 复合，义为「棱皮龟」

senses.title: Material made from animal skin
senses.definition: material made by treating the skin of animals so that it is soft and strong
senses.definitionCN: 把动物皮处理得柔软结实之后得到的材料
senses.example: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。
senses.why: Old English leþer named the treated hide itself, and that material sense has stayed the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leþer 指处理过的兽皮本身，这层材料义一直是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Articles made of leather
senses.definition: things made from leather, especially when spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用皮革制成的物品，尤指用复数形式时
senses.example: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。
senses.why: Because a material can stand for the things cut from it, tanned skins become leathers in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 材料可以代替用它制成的东西，鞣好的皮在复数里就成了皮衣、皮具。

senses.title: Used before a noun to mean made of leather
senses.definition: placed before another noun to say that the thing is made of leather
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示该物由皮革制成
senses.example: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。
senses.why: English often lets a material noun work as a modifier, so leather needs no suffix to describe a jacket.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让材料名词直接作修饰语，所以 leather 不加后缀就能修饰 jacket。

intro.en: An Old English noun for treated hide is the direct source, and its Germanic shape is still easy to hear.
intro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的古英语名词是直接来源，它的日耳曼语形态至今仍容易辨认。

items.en: Leþer named the skin of an animal after treatment, and it is the direct source of the word.
items.cn: leþer 指处理之后的兽皮，是这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The Germanic form behind it is reconstructed as leþra-, with related words in other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其背后的日耳曼语形式被重构为 leþra-，在其他日耳曼语言里有相关词。

items.en: The old word may be related to the idea of a hide, though the exact link is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个旧词可能与「兽皮」的观念有关，但具体联系并不确定。

items.en: Middle English kept leather for the material and began using it for goods made of it.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 leather 指材料，并开始用它指由它制成的物品。

items.en: Modern English uses leather for the material, for leather goods, and as a word placed before nouns.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leather 指材料、指皮具，也把它放在名词前作修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built from leather and words with a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for skins and leather types.
note.cn: 形近组收由 leather 构成的形式以及形状相近的词；近义组收表示兽皮与皮革种类的其他用词。

entries.definition: Tough and dry like leather.
entries.definitionCN: 像皮革一样坚韧干燥。

entries.definition: A manufactured material made to look like leather.
entries.definitionCN: 做成皮革样子的人造材料。

entries.definition: The state of the air outside, sun, rain or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 户外空气的状态，晴、雨或风；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: One of the light growths covering a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖鸟类身体的轻软生成物之一。

entries.definition: The skin of a large animal, raw or tanned.
entries.definitionCN: 大型动物的皮，生的或鞣过的。

entries.definition: The outer covering of a body, or material from it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的外层覆盖物，或由此得来的材料。

entries.definition: Leather with a soft brushed surface.
entries.definitionCN: 表面经过打磨起绒的软革。

entries.definition: The soft hair covering an animal, or a coat made of it.
entries.definitionCN: 动物身上的软毛，或由此制成的衣物。

normalIntro.en: A noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds hold this word together.
normalIntro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的名词，与四个造出性质、仿制品及复合词的英语词尾，共同支撑着这个词。

normal.en: Old English leþer is the direct source, and the th sound in the middle has never changed.
normal.cn: 古英语 leþer 是直接来源，中间那个 th 音一直没变。

normal.en: Leathery adds -y: having the toughness and dryness of leather.
normal.cn: leathery 加 -y，意为具有皮革的坚韧与干燥。

normal.en: Leatherette adds -ette, a suffix for imitations, so it is leather that is not leather.
normal.cn: leatherette 加 -ette，这是表示仿制品的后缀，所以是「不是皮革的皮革」。

normal.en: Leatherback is leather plus back, naming a turtle with a tough shell instead of hard plates.
normal.cn: leatherback 是 leather 加 back，指背甲坚韧而非硬板的龟。

normal.en: In a leather jacket, leather works as a modifier without any suffix.
normal.cn: 在 a leather jacket 里，leather 不加后缀就作修饰语。

abstract.en: A material word can name the goods made from it, so leathers means leather clothes.
abstract.cn: 材料词可以指用它做成的东西，所以 leathers 指皮衣。

abstract.en: Toughness is the memory of a hide that had to protect an animal, carried into a jacket.
abstract.cn: 坚韧是兽皮曾保护过动物的记忆，被带进了一件夹克。

abstract.en: English rarely marks material with a suffix, so leather sits before a noun and quietly becomes an adjective.
abstract.cn: 英语很少用后缀标记材料，于是 leather 直接站在名词前，悄悄变成形容词。

examples.en: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
examples.cn: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。

examples.en: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
examples.cn: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。

examples.en: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
examples.cn: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累着」——皮衣厚重，穿着走一天累着了；记住 leather 是皮革。

root: 古英语 leþer（处理过的兽皮），与日耳曼语中重构的 leþra- 同源；与拉丁语 corium 无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is treated animal skin; the senses then add the plural goods made from it and its use as a word before nouns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是处理过的兽皮；义项由此加上用复数表示的皮具，以及放在名词前作修饰的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tanned hide spread on a wooden bench, a knife at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：木台上摊开的鞣制兽皮，边缘搁着裁皮刀。

branches.en: a hide being worked with a knife on a bench
branches.cn: 木台上被刀修整的兽皮

branches.en: a row of leather jackets hanging in a shop
branches.cn: 店里挂着的一排皮衣

branches.en: a jacket described by the material it is cut from
branches.cn: 用其材料来描述的夹克

branches.en: a wallet softened by years in a pocket
branches.cn: 在口袋里磨软的钱包

branches.en: a belt with a worn buckle, still strong
branches.cn: 扣子磨旧却仍结实的皮带

intro.en: An Old English noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds.

items.meaningCN: leather 与 back 复合，指一种龟

definition_zh: 离开；留下；留给；许可；休假
definition_en: to go away from a place, to let something remain, to give something to someone, or permission and time off
core_image: 一只手松开门把，另一只手把钥匙留在桌上
scene: 清晨的宿舍里，行李箱已经拉到门口。He left the keys on the desk and closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「留下」（第 2 个义项：动词，指让某物继续留在原处）；句意为他先把钥匙留在桌上，然后关上门。图中可辨识物件：行李箱、桌上的钥匙、半开的门。

derivatives.zh: 由 leave 加 -er 构成，义为「离开的人；离校者」
由 left 与 over 复合，义为「剩饭；剩余的」
由 leave 加 -ings 构成，义为「残渣；剩余物」

senses.title: To go away from a place or person
senses.definition: to go away from a place, person or situation
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方、一个人或一种处境走开
senses.example: The train leaves at six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车六点出发。
senses.why: The departing sense grew out of 'leave something behind'; to go is to make a place stay behind you.
senses.whyCN: 「离开」义是从「把某物留在身后」长出来的：走开，就是让那个地方留在你身后。

senses.title: To let something remain
senses.definition: to put or allow something to stay where it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在原处，或让它继续留在那里
senses.example: He left the keys on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙留在了桌上。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: to leave is to let a thing remain, not to move it away.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最早的义项：leave 是让某物留在原处，而不是把它带走。

senses.title: To give something to someone after one's death
senses.definition: to give property or money to someone in a will
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗嘱把财产或钱留给某人
senses.example: She left the house to her nephew.
senses.exampleCN: 她把房子留给了侄子。
senses.why: A bequest is the final form of letting something remain: the owner goes, but the property is left in place for another.
senses.whyCN: 遗赠是「让某物留下」的最终形态：主人走了，财产却留在原处归别人。

senses.title: Permission
senses.definition: permission to do something, especially in formal or official language
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的许可，尤用于正式或官方语境
senses.example: You have my leave to go.
senses.exampleCN: 我允许你去。
senses.why: The permission sense comes from a separate Old English noun lēaf, which simply meant authorization.
senses.whyCN: 许可义来自另一个古英语名词 lēaf，本义就是「授权」。

senses.title: Time away from duty
senses.definition: an authorized period of absence from work or military duty
senses.definitionCN: 获准离开工作或军务的一段时间
senses.example: He is on leave until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他休假到周五。
senses.why: Time off is permission made into a period: the noun of authorization comes to name the absence it allows.
senses.whyCN: 休假是把许可变成一段时间：表示授权的名词转而指它所允许的缺席。

intro.en: Two Old English strands meet in leave: one about letting something remain, one about permission; both survive in modern English.
intro.cn: leave 由两支古英语线索汇合而成：一支关于「让某物留下」，一支关于「许可」，两者都活在现代英语里。

items.en: Læfan meant to let something remain, to leave it behind.
items.cn: læfan 意为让某物留下、把它留在身后。

items.en: Lēaf meant permission or authorization, and it is the source of the noun leave.
items.cn: lēaf 意为许可、授权，是名词 leave 的来源。

items.en: Middle English leven develops the sense of departing, from the idea of leaving a place behind.
items.cn: 中古英语 leven 从「把某地留在身后」发展出「离开」义。

items.en: The permission noun and the departure verb become firmly joined in spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 表示许可的名词与表示离开的动词在十六世纪于拼写和读音上牢固地合流。

items.en: Modern English keeps leave, left and the fixed phrases leave behind and on leave.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 leave、left，以及 leave behind、on leave 等固定短语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections and compounds of leave; the near-meaning group gathers words for departing and quitting.
note.cn: 形近组收 leave 的变形与复合词；近义组收表示离开、放弃的词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of leave.
entries.definitionCN: leave 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: The act of going away.
entries.definitionCN: 离开；离去。

entries.definition: Something that remains after the rest is used.
entries.definitionCN: 剩饭；剩余的。

entries.definition: A person who leaves, especially a school.
entries.definitionCN: 离开者；离校生。

entries.definition: To leave, especially on a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 离开；出发。

entries.definition: To leave a job or place permanently.
entries.definitionCN: 辞职；永久离开。

entries.definition: To leave someone or something behind for good.
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃；遗弃。

entries.definition: To go out of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 退出；离开。

normalIntro.en: Two histories share one spelling, and the past form left is also the word for the opposite of right.
normalIntro.cn: 两段历史共享一个拼写，过去式 left 又恰好是表示「左」的词。

normal.en: The past of leave is left: leave, left, left.
normal.cn: leave 的过去式是 left：leave、left、left。

normal.en: Leave behind means to forget or abandon something.
normal.cn: leave behind 意为落下或丢下某物。

normal.en: Sick leave and on leave use the permission sense of the noun.
normal.cn: sick leave 与 on leave 用的是名词的「许可、休假」义。

normal.en: Leave alone means not to disturb someone.
normal.cn: leave alone 意为不打扰某人。

normal.en: Left as 'the left side' is a different word that happens to share the spelling.
normal.cn: 表示「左边」的 left 是另一个词，只是拼写相同。

abstract.en: The same verb means both going away and letting stay, because every departure chooses what to carry and what to leave.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既指走开，也指让某物留下，因为每次离开都要选择带走什么、留下什么。

abstract.en: Permission and departure share a spelling, as if leaving were something one is allowed to do.
abstract.cn: 许可与离开共享拼写，仿佛离开是一件需要被允许的事。

abstract.en: To leave something to someone is to keep it in place past your own going.
abstract.cn: 把东西留给某人，就是让它在你离开之后仍留在原处。

examples.en: He left the keys on the desk and closed the door.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙留在桌上，然后关上了门。

examples.en: The train leaves at six.
examples.cn: 火车六点出发。

examples.en: She left the house to her nephew.

sensesIntro.en: The core is letting something stay behind; movement away and bequest grow from it, while permission forms a separate strand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「让某物留在身后」；离开与遗赠由此长出，许可则是另一条独立线索。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开门的把手，钥匙仍留在桌上。

branches.en: a train pulling out of a quiet platform
branches.cn: 从安静站台驶出的火车

branches.cn: 灯下留在桌上的钥匙

branches.cn: 批准离岗的签字条

branches.cn: 同一种「留下」，一次是片刻，一次是永远

intro.cn: 两个古英语词干、一个不规则过去式，以及三个英语后缀支撑这个词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

items.meaning: to depart or let remain; permission

definition_zh: 讲座；授课；（大学的）课时；讲稿；训斥
definition_en: a formal talk given to teach or inform, a course session built on such talks, the written text of a talk, a serious scolding, or, in older use, the act of reading
core_image: 讲台前的一束光：把文字拣出来，念给台下的人听
scene: 大学阶梯教室里，教授把讲义摊在讲台上。He began a lecture on the history of the city, and the students below wrote so fast that their pens never stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 lecture 是「讲座、课堂讲授」（第 2 个义项：面向听众的正式讲授）；句意：他开始一场关于城市史的讲座，下面学生的笔一直没停。图中可辨识物件：阶梯教室、讲台、摊开的讲义、投影幕、学生的笔记本。

pos.zh: 讲座；授课；（大学的）课时；讲稿；训斥

derivatives.zh: 讲师；授课者
讲师职位；讲席
授课；讲学

senses.title: Reading aloud: the act of reading
senses.definition: the act of reading a text, especially aloud and in a formal setting (now archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 阅读文本的行为，尤指在正式场合朗读（现已古旧）
senses.example: In the monastery the lecture of the psalm began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院里，晨祷时对圣咏的诵读从黎明开始。
senses.why: Lecture came from Medieval Latin lectura, 'a reading'. Before it named a talk, it named the act of reading itself, and the oldest English examples keep that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: lecture 来自中世纪拉丁语 lectura“阅读”。在它指“讲座”之前，它指的就是“读”这个行为，最早的英语用例保留着这层朴素含义。

senses.title: A formal talk that teaches
senses.titleCN: 讲座：面向听众的正式讲授
senses.definition: a formal talk given to a group of people, especially students, in order to teach or inform them
senses.definitionCN: 为教授或告知一群人（尤指学生）而作的正式讲话
senses.example: She went to a lecture on the history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她去听了一场关于这座城市历史的讲座。
senses.why: In the 16c a lecture was a discourse read or delivered before an audience. The act of reading aloud turned into the public teaching talk, which is now the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 在 16 世纪，lecture 指向听众读出或讲出的一段论述。“朗读”这个动作由此变成公开的教学讲话，也就是今天最核心的义项。

senses.title: A course unit: one class in a series
senses.titleCN: 课时：课程中的一个讲授单元
senses.definition: a single period of instruction in a course, or the course seen as a series of such talks
senses.definitionCN: 课程中的一节讲授，或由一系列讲授构成的整门课
senses.example: The course consists of twelve lectures and four seminars.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课由十二次讲授和四次研讨课组成。
senses.why: Once a lecture is put on a timetable, the talk becomes the unit of a course. Attendance is counted in lectures, and the syllabus is divided into them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦讲座被排进课表，这场讲话就成了课程的计量单位。出勤按“讲”计算，教学大纲也按讲次划分。

senses.title: The written text of a talk
senses.titleCN: 讲稿：写在纸上的那份讲授
senses.definition: the written text or full notes from which a talk is delivered, or a published version of it
senses.definitionCN: 演讲所依据的书面文本或完整讲稿，也指其出版形式
senses.example: She wrote out the lecture in full before rehearsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把讲稿完整写出来，再开始排练。
senses.why: A talk can be fixed on paper before or after it is spoken. The same noun then names the script the speaker holds, which is why one can write, revise or print a lecture.
senses.whyCN: 讲话在说之前或之后都可以固定在纸上。同一个名词于是也指讲者手里的稿子，所以说“写讲稿、改讲稿、印讲稿”都成立。

senses.title: A serious scolding
senses.definition: a long, serious talk to someone about their behaviour, given as a warning or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 就某人的行为作长时间严肃谈话，作为警告或惩罚
senses.example: His father gave him a lecture about wasting money.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲就乱花钱的事训了他一顿。
senses.why: The instructive frame is now aimed at correction. The content is still teaching, but the listener is being told off, so praise and warning replace neutral explanation.
senses.whyCN: 讲授的框架这时对准了“纠正”：内容仍是在教，但听者是在挨批评，于是中性的讲解换成了告诫与责难。

senses.title: Verb: teach by giving talks
senses.definition: to give a formal talk to students or to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 给学生或听众作正式讲授
senses.example: Professor Lin lectures on constitutional history.
senses.exampleCN: 林教授讲授宪政史。
senses.why: This is zero derivation: the noun became a verb with no added suffix, naming the activity of the person behind the lectern.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：名词不加任何后缀直接变成动词，指讲台后面那个人所做的事。

senses.title: Verb: scold at length
senses.definition: to talk seriously and at length to someone about something they have done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就某人做错的事进行长时间严肃谈话
senses.example: The coach lectured the team for giving up in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因球队下半场放弃而训了他们一顿。
senses.why: The verb takes the corrective branch too. Now it has a target and a fault, and the length of the talk is part of the reproach.
senses.whyCN: 动词也接上了“纠正”这一支：此时它带有对象和过错，而“讲得很长”本身就是责难的一部分。

senses.title: A public lecture as an event
senses.titleCN: 公开讲座：作为活动的讲演
senses.definition: a public talk organized as an event, often by a university, museum or learned society
senses.definitionCN: 作为活动组织的公开演讲，常由大学、博物馆或学术团体举办
senses.example: The museum's annual lecture drew an audience of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的年度讲座吸引了五百名听众。
senses.why: The form spreads beyond the classroom. A lecture can now be an event with a title, a guest speaker and tickets, even when no course is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这种形式走出了课堂。lecture 现在可以是一场有标题、有嘉宾讲者、需要门票的活动，即使并不附属于任何课程。

intro.en: Lecture is a reading word before it is a teaching word. Latin legere 'to read' goes back to 'pick out, gather', and English first used lecture for the act of reading, then for the talk.
intro.cn: lecture 先是“阅读”词，后来才是“教学”词。拉丁语 legere“读”的本义是“拣出、采集”；英语先用它指阅读行为，再指讲授。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'the act of reading, a reading aloud', borrowed from Medieval Latin lectura.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语，意为“阅读行为、朗读”，借自中世纪拉丁语 lectura。

items.en: lectura 'a reading' is a noun of action from lectus, the past participle of legere 'to read'.
items.cn: lectura“阅读”是由 legere“读”的过去分词 lectus 构成的行为名词。

items.en: legere meant 'to read', but its older sense was 'to pick out, select, gather'. Reading is pictured as picking out letters one by one from the page.
items.cn: legere 意为“读”，更早的意思是“拣出、挑选、采集”。阅读被想象成从页面上把字母一个个拣出来。

items.en: legere is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather, pick out'. The step from 'gather' to 'read' is inferred rather than attested, so this deeper link is generally accepted.
items.cn: legere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集、拣出”。从“采集”到“读”这一步是推论而非有据可查，因此这层更深的联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: The sense 'a discourse read or delivered before an audience' appears in the 16c. By the 17c lecture is the ordinary word for a university talk, and the old 'reading' sense fades.
items.cn: “向听众读出或讲出的一段论述”这一义项见于 16 世纪。到 17 世纪，lecture 已是大学讲课的常用词，旧的“阅读”义逐渐退场。

items.en: Lecture and legal are not the same family: legere is the verb 'to read', while lex (genitive legis) is the noun 'law'. Both contain the leg- shape and are traced to *leg- 'gather', but law is not a form of 'read'.
items.cn: lecture 与 legal 并非同一家族：legere 是动词“读”，lex（属格 legis）是名词“法”。两者都含 leg- 这一形，都被追溯到 *leg-“采集”，但“法”并不是“读”的某种形式。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the reading root legere from the law noun lex. The near-meaning group separates a teaching talk from other kinds of public speech.
note.cn: 形近组把“读”的词根 legere 与“法”的名词 lex 分开；近义组把教学性讲授与其他类型的公开讲话分开。

entries.definition: a stand for a book or notes, used by someone who is reading or speaking. It comes from the same legere 'read' family, not from lecture itself.
entries.definitionCN: 供朗读或演讲者放置书本、讲稿的架子。它出自同一个 legere“读”的词族，而不是由 lecture 派生。

entries.definition: clear enough to be read. It is legere plus -ibilis 'able to be', so it describes writing that can be read, not a talk that is given.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚、可辨认的。它是 legere 加 -ibilis“能够被……”，形容文字可读，而不是形容所作的讲座。

entries.definition: the body that makes laws. It looks as if it contains lecture's root, but it is lex 'law' plus lator 'proposer', so the meaning is law-making, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关。它看起来含有 lecture 的词根，其实是 lex“法”加 lator“提出者”，所以意思是立法，而不是阅读。

entries.definition: a formal address to an audience. It is broader than lecture and need not teach anything; a lecture is expected to inform.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。它比 lecture 宽泛，不必包含教学；而 lecture 默认要传递知识。

entries.definition: a class in which a small group discusses a topic. It is interactive and smaller, while a lecture is one voice addressing many.
entries.definitionCN: 小组讨论某个主题的课程。它强调互动且人数少，而 lecture 是一个声音对许多人讲。

entries.definition: a talk on a religious or moral theme, usually delivered in worship. It aims at the conscience, not at course content.
entries.definitionCN: 关于宗教或道德主题的讲话，通常在礼拜中宣讲。它对准的是良知，而不是课程内容。

entries.definition: a formal or official rebuke. It is usually shorter and more procedural than a lecture, which explains and moralizes at length.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方的斥责。它通常比 lecture 短、更讲程序，而 lecture 会长篇解释并说教。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: legere 'read', its past participle lectus, and the English family lectern, legible, legend and lesson.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：legere“读”、它的过去分词 lectus，以及英语中的 lectern、legible、legend、lesson。

normal.en: legere 'to read' gives the lect- stem; lecture is literally 'a reading' before it is a talk.
normal.cn: legere“读”给出 lect- 这个词干；lecture 字面上就是“一次阅读”，之后才成为“讲座”。

normal.en: lectern, legible, legend and lesson all come from the same 'read / pick out' family, so the reading image is still visible around lecture.
normal.cn: lectern、legible、legend、lesson 都出自同一个“读／拣出”词族，因此“阅读”的意象在 lecture 周围仍然看得见。

normal.en: The old sense 'a reading' explains why a lecture was once something read aloud rather than freely spoken.
normal.cn: 古义“一次阅读”解释了为什么 lecture 早先是“朗读出来的东西”，而不是即兴讲话。

normal.en: lecture notes and lecture hall keep the classroom frame: notes record the talk, the hall houses it.
normal.cn: lecture notes 与 lecture hall 保留着课堂框架：笔记记录讲授，讲堂容纳讲授。

normal.en: give somebody a lecture moves the same talk from teaching to correcting, which is why the verb can mean 'scold'.
normal.cn: give somebody a lecture 把同一场讲话从“教”移到“纠正”，所以动词可以表示“训斥”。

abstract.en: Picture a page under a lamp: letters are picked out one by one, then the same words are spoken to rows of listeners. Lecture is that page becoming a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象台灯下的一页纸：字母被一个个拣出来，随后同一串词被念给一排排听众。lecture 就是那页纸变成声音的过程。

abstract.en: The voice can teach or scold; only the listener's posture changes — a notebook open, or a head held down.
abstract.cn: 同一个声音可以教人，也可以训人；变的只是听者的姿态——要么摊开笔记本，要么低着头。

abstract.en: A lecture is a text that has learned to stand up and speak, and a course is a row of such texts standing in line.
abstract.cn: 一场 lecture 是一段学会站起来说话的文字，而一门课程就是这样的文字排成一列。

examples.en: The lecture on volcanoes was full of photographs from the 1980 eruption.
examples.cn: 那场关于火山的讲座满是 1980 年喷发的照片。

examples.en: He lectures to first-year students three mornings a week.
examples.cn: 他每周有三个上午给一年级学生授课。

examples.en: My mother lectured me for twenty minutes about the unpaid bill.
examples.cn: 母亲为那张没付的账单训了我二十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来课扯”——上课时把内容扯成一大段 → lecture 讲座、训斥

root: 拉丁语 legere“读”（本义“采集、挑选”）→ 中世纪拉丁 lectura“阅读”，核心是“把文字拣出来、念给人听”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lecture, one movement: a text is picked out and read, the reading becomes a talk, the talk becomes a course unit and a script, and finally the same instructive voice turns into a scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: lecture 的八个义项是一条运动线：文字被拣出来读，读变成讲授，讲授变成课时与讲稿，最后同一种“教导口吻”变成训斥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words are picked out of a page and spoken to people who came to listen.
core.cn: 核心意象：把字从纸页上拣出来，念给前来听的人。

branches.en: READING: the oldest layer, when lecture names the act of reading rather than a talk.
branches.cn: 阅读：最古老的一层，此时 lecture 指的是“读”这一行为，而不是讲座。

branches.en: INSTRUCTION: the classroom talk, the verb for giving it, and the public lecture as an event.
branches.cn: 讲授：课堂讲座、表示“讲授”的动词，以及作为活动的公开讲座。

branches.en: COURSE UNIT: the talk becomes a countable slot in a timetable and a syllabus.
branches.cn: 课时：讲座变成课表与教学大纲里可计数的一格。

branches.en: WRITTEN TEXT: the spoken words are fixed on paper as a script or a printed talk.
branches.cn: 书面文本：说出的话被固定在纸上，成为讲稿或印行的讲辞。

branches.en: CORRECTION: the instructive voice turns into a long scolding, as a noun and as a verb.
branches.cn: 纠正：教导的口吻变成长篇训斥，名词与动词都走这一支。

intro.en: Lecture is a borrowed Latin noun, not a prefixed English word. English adds only ordinary suffixes: -er for the person, -ship for the post, -ing for the activity; the noun also became a verb with no suffix at all.
intro.cn: lecture 是借入的拉丁名词，不是由英语前缀构成的词。英语只加普通后缀：-er 表人，-ship 表职位，-ing 表活动；名词还零派生成了动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base legere 'read / pick out' has a large family. Note that lex 'law' is a different noun with a similar shape, and legare 'send, bequeath' is a different verb again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 legere“读／拣出”有一个很大的词族。注意 lex“法”是形似的另一个名词，legare“派出、遗赠”又是另一个动词。

items.meaning: a person who gives lectures, especially at a university
items.meaningCN: 讲师；授课者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The lecturer paused to answer a question.
items.exampleCN: 讲师停下来回答了一个问题。

items.meaning: the post or position of a lecturer
items.meaningCN: 讲师职位；讲席（-ship 表示职位或身份）
items.example: She was appointed to a lectureship in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获聘物理学讲师职位。

items.meaningCN: 授课；讲学（-ing 构成行为名词）
items.example: His lecturing took him to six countries.
items.exampleCN: 他的讲学让他去了六个国家。

items.meaning: to give a lecture; to scold at length
items.meaningCN: 讲授；长篇训斥（名动同形，不加后缀）

items.meaning: to read; to pick out, gather
items.example: The verb is the root shared by lecture, lector and collect.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 lecture、lector、collect 共有的词根。

items.example: Every English word on this stem keeps the reading image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干上的英语词都保留“读”的意象。

items.example: It turns the act of reading into the noun lecture.
items.exampleCN: 它把“读”的动作变成名词 lecture。

items.meaning: a reader; one who reads aloud in a service
items.meaningCN: 诵读者；（礼拜中的）读经员
items.example: The lector read the passage aloud to the congregation.
items.exampleCN: 读经员向会众朗读了那段经文。

items.structure: Medieval Latin lectrum, from the stem lect-
items.meaning: a reading desk, especially in a church
items.example: She set her notes on the lectern before speaking.
items.exampleCN: 发言前她把讲稿放在讲台上。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be read; clear enough to read
latinEntries.meaningCN: 可读的；字迹清晰的（-ibilis 表“能够被……”）

latinEntries.meaning: a story handed down; originally 'things to be read' about the saints
latinEntries.meaningCN: 传说；原指关于圣徒“应被诵读的事迹”

latinEntries.meaning: a unit of teaching; originally a passage read aloud
latinEntries.meaningCN: 课；原义是“所读的一段文字”

latinEntries.meaning: to bring things together; literally 'to gather up'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 收集；字面义“把东西拣到一起”

definition_zh: 左边的；剩余的；左边；左翼；向左
definition_en: on the side of the body where the heart is not, also what remains after something is taken away, and the political side that sits on that hand
core_image: 一个人伸出左手，掌心向外，拇指指向另一侧
scene: 雨停了，街上的人流分成两股。The shop stands on the left side of the street.
sceneCN: 这里 left 指「左边的」（第 1 个义项）；句意为那家店位于街道的左侧。图中可辨识物件：分流的行人、街口的店铺、指示方向的招牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 left 加 -ist 构成，指左翼人士，也可作形容词
由 left 加 -y 构成，非正式指左撇子或左翼人士
由 left 加 -ward 构成，指朝左的、向左的

senses.title: On the side of the left hand
senses.definition: located on the side of the body where the left hand is, opposite the right
senses.definitionCN: 位于左手所在一侧，与右侧相对
senses.example: The shop stands on the left side of the street.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店位于街道的左侧。
senses.why: The word first described the weaker hand, the one less used for work, and that bodily picture is still the base of the direction sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初形容较弱的那只手，即较少干活的那只，而这幅身体画面至今是方向义的基础。

senses.title: Remaining after something is taken
senses.definition: still there after other parts have been used, taken away or gone
senses.definitionCN: 在其他部分被用掉、拿走或离开之后仍然存在的
senses.example: There is only a little bread left.
senses.exampleCN: 只剩下一点面包了。
senses.why: The form is also the past of leave, so what is left is literally what has been left behind by everyone else.
senses.whyCN: 这个形式同时是 leave 的过去式，所以 what is left 字面上就是被其他人留下的东西。

senses.title: The left side or direction
senses.definition: the side of the body or of a space that lies to the left, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 身体或空间中位于左手一侧的那一边，作名词
senses.example: The post office is on the left.
senses.exampleCN: 邮局在左边。
senses.why: Once the adjective named a side, it could stand alone as a noun, because speakers did not need to repeat the word side.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个形容词指出了一个侧面，它就能单独作名词，因为说话人不必再重复 side 这个词。

senses.title: The political left
senses.definition: the political groups that favour change, equality and state action, seated on the left in many parliaments
senses.definitionCN: 主张变革、平等与国家干预的政治群体，在许多议会中坐在左侧
senses.example: The candidate drew support from the left of the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这位候选人得到了党内左翼的支持。
senses.why: In a French assembly the radicals sat on the king's left, and seating turned a direction word into a name for a political camp.
senses.whyCN: 在法国议会里，激进派坐在国王的左边，座次把方向词变成了一个政治阵营的名称。

senses.title: Toward the left
senses.definition: in the direction of the left side, used as an adverb
senses.definitionCN: 朝左侧的方向，作副词
senses.example: Turn left when you reach the church.
senses.exampleCN: 走到教堂时向左转。
senses.why: When the direction word is used alone with a verb of movement, the adjective becomes an adverb, as in turn left.
senses.whyCN: 当这个方向词单独与表示移动的动词连用时，形容词就变成副词，例如 turn left。

intro.en: Left has two Old English sources that ended up with one spelling: a word for the weak hand, and the past form of a verb meaning to leave behind.
intro.cn: left 有两个古英语来源，最后共用一个拼写：一个指较弱的手，另一个是表示「留下」的动词的过去式。

items.en: Lyft meant weak or idle, and lyft hand named the weaker hand, the one less used for work.
items.cn: lyft 意为虚弱、闲置，lyft hand 指较弱的那只手，即较少干活的那只。

items.en: Lǣfan meant to leave something behind, and its past form left supplied the sense of what remains.
items.cn: lǣfan 意为把东西留下，其过去式 left 提供了「剩余」的意思。

items.en: Middle English kept left for the weak side and for what is left over, and the two words shared one spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语用 left 指较弱的一侧和剩下的东西，两个词共用了一个拼写。

items.en: The political sense appeared later, when the seating of a French assembly put radicals on the king's left.
items.cn: 政治义出现得更晚，源于法国议会坐席把激进派安排在国王左边。

items.en: Modern English uses left for direction, for what remains and for the political side, all from one short spelling.
items.cn: 现代英语的 left 同时指方向、剩余之物与政治左翼，都出自这一个短短的拼写。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on left with suffixes; the near-meaning group collects the opposite direction and words for what remains.
note.cn: 形近组收由 left 加后缀构成的词；近义组收相反方向与表示剩余的词。

entries.definition: A person who supports the political left.
entries.definitionCN: 支持政治左翼的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a left-handed or left-wing person.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用语，指左撇子或左翼人士。

entries.definition: Directed or moving towards the left.
entries.definitionCN: 朝左的、向左移动的。

entries.definition: On the side opposite the left, the other hand of the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 与左侧相对的一边，这一对中的另一只手。

entries.definition: Still present after the rest has gone.
entries.definitionCN: 其余部分离开之后仍然存在的。

entries.definition: Something not used up, often used of food.
entries.definitionCN: 没有用完的东西，常用于食物。

entries.definition: Located on or designed for the left hand side.
entries.definitionCN: 位于左手一侧或供左手使用的。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a weak hand and a leaving behind at once, and modern English reads both as one small spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时带着「较弱的手」与「留下」两层来历，现代英语把它们读成同一个短短的拼写。

normal.en: Left first meant weak, so the left hand was simply the hand that did less work.
normal.cn: left 最初意为虚弱，所以左手就是干活较少的那只手。

normal.en: The past of leave is left, so what is left has literally been left behind.
normal.cn: leave 的过去式是 left，所以剩下的东西字面上就是被留下来的。

normal.en: On the left works because the adjective could stand alone once the side was obvious.
normal.cn: on the left 成立，是因为一侧已经明确时形容词可以单独使用。

normal.en: Turn left uses the same word as an adverb of direction.
normal.cn: turn left 用的是同一个词，作方向副词。

normal.en: The political left comes from seating: radicals sat on the king's left in a French assembly.
normal.cn: 政治左翼来自座次：法国议会里激进派坐在国王左边。

abstract.en: One spelling holds two unrelated histories, which is why left can mean both a side and a remainder.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写装着两段互不相关的历史，所以 left 既能指一边，也能指剩余。

abstract.en: A direction word becomes a political label the moment people arrange themselves in a room.
abstract.cn: 一旦人们在房间里排好座位，方向词就变成了政治标签。

abstract.en: What is left is not a failure but a fact: something stayed when everything else moved.
abstract.cn: 剩下的东西不是失败而是事实：别的都走了，它还在。

examples.en: The shop stands on the left side of the street.
examples.cn: 那家店位于街道的左侧。

examples.en: There is only a little bread left.
examples.cn: 只剩下一点面包了。

examples.en: The candidate drew support from the left of the party.
examples.cn: 这位候选人得到了党内左翼的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福」——左手边来福气；谐音记住 left 是左边、剩余。

root: 有两个来源：古英语 lyft（虚弱、闲置）构成「左手」义；古英语 lǣfan（留下）的过去式 left 构成「剩余」义。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the weaker-hand side; the same spelling also carries what is left behind, and from these grow the noun, the adverb and the political label.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是较弱的手所在一侧；同一拼写又带着「留下来的东西」，名词、副词与政治标签都由这两者生长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding out the left hand, thumb pointing away from the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伸出左手，拇指指向身体外侧。

branches.en: a shop standing on one side of a street
branches.cn: 街道一侧的店铺

branches.en: a few slices of bread on a plate
branches.cn: 盘子里剩下的几片面包

branches.en: radicals seated together in an assembly
branches.cn: 议会里坐在一起激进派

branches.en: a hand pointing the way at a corner
branches.cn: 街角指路的手

branches.en: a post office on the left of a square
branches.cn: 广场左边的邮局

intro.en: English builds the family of left with -ist, -y and -ward, while the base word itself comes from two Old English sources.
intro.cn: 英语用 -ist、-y 与 -ward 扩展 left 的词族，而基础词本身来自两个古英语来源。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for left; both of its Old English sources are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: left 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它的两个古英语来源都属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 腿；裤腿；家具的腿；（行程的）一段
definition_en: one of the limbs used for standing and walking; the part of a garment covering it; a support of furniture; one stage of a journey or race
core_image: 人迈步时，一条腿稳稳撑住身体
scene: 翻越栅栏时，他的小腿磕在木桩上，裤腿也被划开一道口子。He hurt his leg while jumping over the fence.
sceneCN: 这里是「腿」（第 1 个义项：人或动物的下肢）；句意是他翻越栅栏时伤了腿。图中可辨识物件：木栅栏、裤腿、划破的布料。

pos.zh: 腿；裤腿；家具的腿；（行程的）一段

derivatives.zh: 由 leg 加 -ed 构成，义为「有腿的；……条腿的」
由 leg 加 -ing 与复数 -s 构成，义为「紧身裤；绑腿」
由 leg 加 -less 构成，义为「无腿的；酩酊大醉的」

senses.title: A limb used for standing and walking
senses.definition: one of the limbs of a person or animal used for standing and walking
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物用来站立和行走的肢体之一
senses.example: He hurt his leg while jumping over the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他翻越栅栏时伤了腿。
senses.why: The Old Norse word named the limb and also the stem of a plant, and the bodily sense remains the centre of the English word.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语这个词既指肢体，也指植物的茎，而身体义仍是英语这个词的中心。

senses.title: The part of a garment that covers a leg
senses.definition: the part of trousers or another garment that covers one leg
senses.definitionCN: 裤子或其他衣物覆盖一条腿的部分
senses.example: One leg of his trousers was muddy from the knee down.
senses.exampleCN: 他的一条裤腿从膝盖往下全是泥。
senses.why: Clothing copies the body it covers, so the tube around a leg naturally takes the name of the leg itself.
senses.whyCN: 衣物照着它所覆盖的身体成形，所以包住腿的那截管子自然沿用腿的名字。

senses.title: A support on which furniture stands
senses.definition: one of the upright supports on which a table, chair or other piece of furniture stands
senses.definitionCN: 桌、椅等家具站立所依靠的直立支撑之一
senses.example: The table wobbles because one leg is shorter than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子晃，因为一条腿比别的短。
senses.why: A support under a table does the same job as a leg under a body: it holds the thing up, which is why the word transfers.
senses.whyCN: 桌下的支撑与身体下的腿做同样的工作：把东西撑住，所以这个词被转用过去。

senses.title: One stage of a journey or race
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a journey or race is divided
senses.definitionCN: 旅程或比赛被分成的若干段之一
senses.example: The last leg of the trip took us through the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 旅程的最后一段带我们穿过了群山。
senses.why: A journey is walked one stretch at a time, and each stretch is like a step taken with a leg, so the word marks a stage of movement.
senses.whyCN: 旅程是一段一段走完的，每一段都像用腿迈出的一步，于是这个词被用来标记移动的一个阶段。

intro.en: Leg came into English from Old Norse, replacing older English words for the limb; English then extended it to trousers, furniture and stages of travel.
intro.cn: leg 从古诺斯语进入英语，取代了更古老的英语肢体词；英语随后把它扩展到裤腿、家具和行程阶段。

items.en: A related Germanic form is reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中可重构出一个相关形式，但确切形态并不确定。

items.en: The Old Norse word leggr named the leg and also the stem of a plant.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 leggr 既指腿，也指植物的茎。

items.en: Middle English adopted leg from Scandinavian speech and used it beside the older English word shank.
items.cn: 中古英语从斯堪的纳维亚语借入 leg，与更古老的英语词 shank 并用。

items.en: Early modern English extended leg to the legs of furniture and to the legs of trousers.
items.cn: 早期现代英语把 leg 扩展到家具腿和裤腿。

items.en: Modern English also uses leg for one stage of a journey or race, especially in travel and sport.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 leg 指旅程或比赛中的一段，尤见于旅行与体育。

note.en: The look-alike group collects suffixes and compounds built on leg; the near-meaning group collects other limbs and supports.
note.cn: 形近组收由 leg 构成的后缀词与复合词；近义组收其他肢体与支撑物。

entries.definition: Having legs, often of a stated number or kind.
entries.definitionCN: 有腿的，常与数字或种类连用，如「三条腿的」。

entries.definition: Tight trousers or coverings for the legs, often worn for exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 紧贴腿部的裤子或护腿，常于运动时穿。

entries.definition: Without legs, or, in informal British English, very drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 没有腿的；英式口语中也指酩酊大醉。

entries.definition: Space in which to put your legs when seated.
entries.definitionCN: 坐着时放腿的空间。

entries.definition: An arm, leg or wing considered as a separate part of the body.
entries.definitionCN: 作为身体独立部分的一条臂、腿或翅。

entries.definition: The upper part of the leg, between hip and knee.
entries.definitionCN: 腿的上部，位于髋与膝之间。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the leg, used for standing.
entries.definitionCN: 腿末端用来站立的部分。

entries.definition: The lower part of the leg, or an older English word for the leg.
entries.definitionCN: 小腿部分，或英语中较古老的「腿」的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word came from Norse and stayed concrete; suffixes count legs or remove them, and compounds name space and clothing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自古诺斯语，始终很具体；后缀数出腿或去掉腿，复合词则命名空间与衣物。

normal.en: Leg entered English from Old Norse leggr, which is why it replaced rather than descended from the old English word shank.
normal.cn: leg 从古诺斯语 leggr 进入英语，所以它是取代而非继承古英语词 shank。

normal.en: Legged adds -ed and usually needs a number: a three-legged stool has three legs.
normal.cn: legged 加 -ed，通常要与数字连用：three-legged stool 就是三条腿的凳子。

normal.en: Leggings adds -ing and a plural to name garments that cover the legs tightly.
normal.cn: leggings 加 -ing 与复数，指紧包腿部的衣物。

normal.en: Legless adds -less: without legs, and by informal extension, too drunk to stand.
normal.cn: legless 加 -less：没有腿，并引申为醉得站不住。

normal.en: Legroom is leg plus room, the space a seated person needs for the legs.
normal.cn: legroom 是 leg 加 room，指坐着的人放腿所需的空间。

abstract.en: A leg both holds a body up and moves it forward, and those two jobs explain the furniture and journey senses.
abstract.cn: 腿既撑住身体又推动身体前进，这两项工作分别解释了家具义和行程义。

abstract.en: Clothing that wraps a limb borrows the limb's name, showing how language lets objects copy the body.
abstract.cn: 包住肢体的衣物借用了肢体的名字，显示语言让物件照着身体命名。

abstract.en: The last leg of a journey is tiring in the same way as the last steps of a long walk.
abstract.cn: 旅程的最后一段，和长途行走的最后几步一样令人疲惫。

examples.en: He hurt his leg while jumping over the fence.
examples.cn: 他翻越栅栏时伤了腿。

examples.en: One leg of his trousers was muddy from the knee down.
examples.cn: 他的一条裤腿从膝盖往下全是泥。

examples.en: The last leg of the trip took us through the mountains.
examples.cn: 旅程的最后一段带我们穿过了群山。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the limb that supports and moves the body; the senses divide into clothing, furniture supports and stages of travel.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是支撑并推动身体的肢体；义项由此分为衣物、家具支撑和行程阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one leg planted firmly as the other swings forward in a step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条腿稳稳撑住，另一条向前迈出。

branches.en: a runner's leg bearing the weight of a stride
branches.cn: 跑者一条承重的腿

branches.cn: 膝盖以下沾泥的裤腿

branches.cn: 撑开地图供最后一段行程使用的支架

intro.cn: 这个古诺斯语名词加上数腿或去腿的后缀，以及与衣物、坐姿空间有关的复合词。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a limb for standing and walking
having legs of a stated kind
the physical effort of gathering information
items.meaningCN: 跑腿的活儿；实地调查工作

definition_zh: 法律的；合法的；法定的；法律上有效的；法律职业的
definition_en: relating to law, allowed or required by law, valid in law, connected with the legal profession, or allowed by the rules of a game
core_image: 一部摊开的法典，页边压着印章：允许什么、要求什么，都写在上面
scene: 律所的会议室里，律师把合同翻到签字页。She pointed out that the clause was not legal in this country and had to be rewritten before anyone could sign.
sceneCN: 这里 legal 是「合法的、法律允许的」（第 2 个义项：为法律所允许）；句意：她指出这一条在本国不合法，必须改写之后才能签字。图中可辨识物件：会议室长桌、合同、签字页、法典、印章。

（美）法定尺寸纸张；法律文件（常用复数 legals）
