senses.title: Relating to law in general
senses.definition: connected with the law, the courts, or the system of rules a society enforces
senses.definitionCN: 与法律、法院或社会所执行的规则体系有关的
senses.example: She is studying the legal systems of two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 她在研究两个国家的法律体系。
senses.why: Legal began as the adjective of Latin lex 'law', so its widest sense simply marks anything belonging to the law as an institution.
senses.whyCN: legal 最初是拉丁语 lex“法”的形容词，因此最宽的义项只是标记“属于法律这个制度”的事物。

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.definition: permitted by law; not forbidden or criminal
senses.definitionCN: 为法律所允许的；未被禁止或不算犯罪的
senses.example: In some states it is legal to record a call you take part in.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些州，录下自己参与的通话是合法的。
senses.why: From 'belonging to law' comes 'consistent with law'. The question is no longer what law is about, but whether an act falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: 从“属于法律”引申出“符合法律”。问题不再是“法管什么”，而是一个行为是否落在被允许的界线之内。

senses.title: Required by law
senses.definition: required or prescribed by law, so that not doing it is a breach
senses.definitionCN: 由法律要求或规定的，不做即构成违法或违约
senses.example: Employers have a legal duty to provide safety training.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主有提供安全培训的法定义务。
senses.why: The same boundary has a second side: what law permits it also commands. A legal duty is not optional, and the adjective shifts from permission to obligation.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线还有另一面：法律允许的东西，也可以被法律命令。legal duty 不是可选项，形容词于是从“许可”滑向“义务”。

senses.title: Valid and enforceable in law
senses.definition: recognized as valid and enforceable by law, especially of a document, contract or claim
senses.definitionCN: 被法律认可为有效且可执行的，尤指文件、合同或主张
senses.example: The contract is not legal without both signatures.
senses.exampleCN: 没有双方签字，这份合同在法律上不生效。
senses.why: Here legal does not mean 'allowed' but 'having legal force'. A document can be legally made yet legally ineffective if a formality is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 legal 不是“被允许”，而是“具有法律效力”。一份文件可以依法制作，却因缺少形式要件而在法律上无效。

senses.title: Of the legal profession
senses.definition: relating to lawyers, their training, or the business of giving legal advice
senses.definitionCN: 与律师、其训练或提供法律意见的业务有关的
senses.example: He left banking for a legal career at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时离开银行业，转做法律职业。
senses.why: The institution is also a trade. Legal then describes the people and practices that operate the system, not the rules themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律这套制度同时也是一门行业。legal 于是描述运作这套制度的人与业务，而不是规则本身。

senses.title: Relating to lawsuits
senses.definition: relating to court proceedings or to action taken through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 与法院程序或通过法院采取的行动有关的
senses.example: The tenants threatened legal action over the mould.
senses.exampleCN: 租户因霉斑问题威胁要采取法律诉讼。
senses.why: One branch of the system is dispute. Legal action names the step from a private quarrel to a case that a court can decide.
senses.whyCN: 这套制度的一支是争端。legal action 标记了从私人纠纷跨到“法院可以裁决的案件”的那一步。

senses.title: According to the letter of the law
senses.definition: existing or holding a status in law, even if the actual situation is different
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上存在或拥有某种身份，即使实际情况不同
senses.example: She is the legal owner, though her brother runs the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她是法律上的所有者，尽管农场由她哥哥经营。
senses.why: Law can assign a name that reality does not match. Legal owner, legal parent and legal fiction all use the adjective to mark the official version, as opposed to the factual one.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以给出一个与现实不符的名义。legal owner、legal parent、legal fiction 都用这个形容词标记“官方版本”，以区别于事实版本。

senses.title: Allowed by the rules of a game
senses.definition: allowed by the rules of a sport or game, though not necessarily by statute
senses.definitionCN: 为运动或游戏规则所允许的，而不一定涉及成文法
senses.example: The tackle was hard but legal.
senses.exampleCN: 那次擒抱很凶，但符合规则。
senses.why: The boundary image is borrowed from law: a game has its own code, and a move inside it is called legal by analogy. Here no court is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这里借用了“界线”的意象：游戏有自己的规则法典，规则内的动作被类比地称为 legal，此时并不涉及法院。

senses.title: Legal-size paper
senses.definition: a US paper size of 8.5 by 14 inches, sold as legal pads and used for long documents
senses.definitionCN: 美国一种 8.5×14 英寸的纸张规格，做成黄色横线稿纸，用于较长的文书
senses.example: He drafted the will on a yellow legal pad.
senses.exampleCN: 他在黄色法定尺寸稿纸上起草了遗嘱。
senses.why: The adjective became a fixed label for a paper size once associated with legal records. This is an attributive use, not a new legal concept.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词固定成了纸张规格的标签，因为这种尺寸曾与法律文书相关。这是定语用法，并不是新的法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a direct Latin borrowing, not a French one: English took legalis from Latin in the 15c, while loyal came through French from the same source. Its noun is lex, not legare and not licere.
intro.cn: legal 是直接借自拉丁语，而非借自法语：英语在 15 世纪直接取用 legalis；loyal 则是同一来源经法语变来的。它的名词是 lex，不是 legare，也不是 licere。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'of or pertaining to law'. It was borrowed straight from Latin legalis rather than through French.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪中期的英语，意为“与法律有关的”。它是直接从拉丁语 legalis 借入的，而不是经法语转手。

items.en: legalis 'of or belonging to the law' is formed from lex (genitive legis) 'law, statute, bill' plus -alis 'relating to'.
items.cn: legalis“属于法律的”由 lex（属格 legis）“法、法规、议案”加 -alis“与……有关的”构成。

items.en: lex is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather'. The idea may be 'that which is collected or laid down', but this semantic step is generally accepted, not documented.
items.cn: lex 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集”。其理据可能是“被收集、被放下之物”，但这一步只是一般认为是，并无文献确证。

items.en: legare 'to send, depute; bequeath' is a different verb, source of legate, legacy and allegation. Its connection with lex is source uncertain, so legal must not be treated as derived from legare.
items.cn: legare“派出、委任；遗赠”是另一个动词，是 legate、legacy、allegation 的来源。它与 lex 的联系来源不确定，因此不能把 legal 当作 legare 的派生词。

items.en: licere 'to be permitted' is a third root, the source of license. Being permitted by someone is not the same as being lawful under a statute.
items.cn: licere“被允许”是第三条词根线，是 license 的来源。被某人允许，与在成文法下合法，并不是同一件事。

items.en: Legal now covers the system, permission, obligation, validity and the profession. Loyal, legate and legacy are close relatives in form but come by different routes, so their meanings must not be merged.
items.cn: 现代 legal 覆盖法律体系、许可、义务、效力和法律职业。loyal、legate、legacy 在形式上亲近，却走了不同路线，词义不可合并。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes three neighbours: one from legere 'read', one genuinely from lex, and one from legare 'bequeath'. The near-meaning group separates permission, justification, statute and the courts.
note.cn: 形近组混入三个邻居：一个出自 legere“读”，一个确实出自 lex，一个出自 legare“遗赠”。近义组则把许可、正当性、成文法与法院区分开。

entries.definition: clear enough to read. It looks like legal but comes from legere 'to read', so it has nothing to do with law.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚可读的。它形似 legal，却出自 legere“读”，与法律无关。

entries.definition: lawful or valid; also reasonable and justified. It comes from Latin legitimus, built on lex, so it is a true cousin of legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合情合理的。它来自以 lex 构成的拉丁语 legitimus，是 legal 真正的同族词。

entries.definition: money or property left to someone by a will. It looks legal, but it comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex 'law'.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱留给某人的钱财或财产。它形似 legal，却出自 legare“遗赠”，而非 lex“法”。

entries.definition: allowed by law; not against the law. It is plainer and older than legal and often carries a moral tone that legal lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；不违法的。它比 legal 更朴素、更古老，常带有 legal 所缺的道德意味。

entries.definition: valid according to law or reason. Unlike legal, it can also mean 'fair and justified' outside any statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依法律或依理性有效的。与 legal 不同，它还可以指任何法规之外的事情“合理、正当”。

entries.definition: required or created by a written statute. It is narrower and more technical than legal, which covers the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 由成文法规定或创设的。它比 legal 更窄、更技术化，因为 legal 覆盖整个法律体系。

entries.definition: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice. It names one branch of the system, not law as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与法院、法官或司法有关的。它指体系中的一个分支，而不是整个法律。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: lex (genitive legis) 'law' + -alis, with legitimate, legislature and loyal in the same family. Watch the false friends legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis，同族有 legitimate、legislature、loyal。要警惕形近假朋友 legere“读”与 legare“遗赠”。

normal.en: lex, legis is the noun 'law'; legalis adds -alis 'relating to'. The core is simply 'of the law'.
normal.cn: lex、legis 是名词“法”；legalis 加上 -alis“与……有关”。核心意思就是“属于法的”。

normal.en: legitimate and legislature are built on the same lex, which is why they all carry a law meaning.
normal.cn: legitimate 与 legislature 都建在同一个 lex 上，所以它们都带“法”的含义。

normal.en: legacy comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex. A legacy is what a will leaves, not what a statute says.
normal.cn: legacy 出自 legare“遗赠”，不是 lex。legacy 是遗嘱留下的东西，不是法规规定的条文。

normal.en: loyal is legalis after its trip through French: same source, different word. Loyalty is faithfulness, not legality.
normal.cn: loyal 是 legalis 经法语旅行后的样子：同源而异词。loyalty 是忠诚，不是合法性。

normal.en: legal age and legal duty show the two sides of the boundary: one permits, the other obliges.
normal.cn: legal age 与 legal duty 展示同一条界线的两面：一面是允许，一面是强制。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a floor: inside it, everything is allowed; on the line, everything is required; outside it, nothing is recognized. Legal is the line itself, seen from any side.
abstract.cn: 想象地板上画的一条线：线内一切被允许，线上一切被要求，线外一切不被承认。legal 就是这条线本身，从哪一面看都算。

abstract.en: The same stamp can mean 'you may', 'you must' or 'this counts', depending on which document it lands on.
abstract.cn: 同一枚印章落在不同文件上，可以表示“你可以”“你必须”或“这份算数”。

abstract.en: Law has a name for things that do not exist in fact: the legal owner is a person the paper sees, not always the person the field sees.
abstract.cn: 法律会为事实上不存在的东西命名：法律上的所有者是纸面看见的人，未必是田里看见的人。

examples.en: The company sought legal advice before signing the deal.
examples.cn: 公司在签署交易前寻求法律咨询。

examples.en: Is it legal to park here after six?
examples.cn: 六点以后在这里停车合法吗？

examples.en: She was the legal owner of the flat but had never lived in it.
examples.cn: 她是这套公寓法律上的所有者，却从未住过。

dict_mnemonic.text: “李哥”——李哥办事只走正规手续 → legal 合法的、法律的

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis“与……有关的”，核心是“写在法典里、有法律依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of legal, all radiating from one noun, lex. A thing can belong to the law, be allowed by it, be required by it, be valid under it, be done by its professionals, or merely carry its label.
sensesIntro.cn: legal 的九个义项都从一个名词 lex 放射出来：某事物可以属于法律、被法律允许、被法律要求、在法律上有效、由法律从业者去做，或只是贴着法律的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line written into a code, marking what is allowed, required and recognized.
core.cn: 核心意象：写进法典的一条界线，标出什么被允许、什么被要求、什么被承认。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PROFESSION: law as an institution, and the people who operate it.
branches.cn: 体系与职业：作为制度的法律，以及运作它的人。

branches.en: PERMISSION: what statute allows, and, by analogy, what the rules of a game allow.
branches.cn: 许可：成文法允许的事，以及类比到游戏规则所允许的事。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: the other side of the boundary, where the law commands rather than permits.
branches.cn: 义务：界线的另一面，法律在这里不是允许而是命令。

branches.en: LEGAL EFFECT: validity, court action, and the official status that may differ from fact.
branches.cn: 法律效力：有效性、诉讼，以及可能与事实不同的官方身份。

branches.en: PAPER SIZE: a fixed attributive use, where the adjective labels a format rather than a legal idea.
branches.cn: 纸张规格：固定的定语用法，形容词在这里标记的是尺寸，而不是法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a Latin adjective borrowed whole. English adds -ly for the adverb, -ity for the abstract noun, -ize for the verb, and the negative prefix il- before l.
intro.cn: legal 是整体借入的拉丁形容词。英语加 -ly 构成副词，-ity 构成抽象名词，-ize 构成动词，并在 l 前用否定前缀 il-。

latinIntro.en: The lex family is wide: legitimate, legislature, loyal and privilege all contain the law noun in different shapes. Keep it apart from legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
latinIntro.cn: lex 词族很宽：legitimate、legislature、loyal、privilege 都以不同形态含有“法”这个名词。要把它与 legere“读”、legare“遗赠”分开。

items.meaning: in a way that is allowed by law; according to law
items.meaningCN: 合法地；在法律上（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 那场抗议是合法举行的。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being legal
items.meaningCN: 合法性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The court questioned the legality of the search.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑那次搜查的合法性。

items.meaning: to make something legal by law
items.example: Several states have legalized recreational use.
items.exampleCN: 有几个州已将娱乐性使用合法化。

items.meaningCN: 非法的；违法的（il- 是否定前缀，用在 l 前）
items.example: It is illegal to dump waste in the river.
items.exampleCN: 向河里倾倒废物是违法的。

items.example: The noun supplies the law at the centre of legal.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 legal 核心的“法”。

items.example: The stem appears in legal, legislate and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 legal、legislate 与 legitimate。

items.example: It turns the noun for law into the adjective legal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“法”这个名词变成形容词 legal。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being
items.example: It forms legality, the quality of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 legality，即合乎法律的性质。

items.meaning: strict adherence to law or to written rules
items.meaningCN: 条文主义；死守法律条文
items.example: Critics say legalism ignores the purpose behind the rule.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说条文主义忽视了规则背后的目的。

latinEntries.meaning: lawful, valid; also reasonable and justified
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合理正当的（词根仍是 lex“法”）

latinEntries.meaning: the body that has power to make laws
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法机关（legis 属格 + lator“提出者”）

latinEntries.meaning: faithful to a ruler, country or promise
latinEntries.meaningCN: 忠诚的；同源于 legalis，经法语音变而成，不是英语 legal 的派生

latinEntries.meaning: a special right; originally a law made for an individual
latinEntries.meaningCN: 特权；原指为某个人制定的法律（privus“个人”+ lex“法”）

definition_zh: 立法；立法行为；法律法规（总称）；（某一部）法律
definition_en: the making of laws by an authorized body, or the body of laws so made
core_image: 议事厅里逐条朗读、举手表决，散会后书记员把通过的条文装订成厚册
scene: 辩论持续到深夜，反对党仍要求把每一条都念完再表决。Parliament passed legislation that rewrites the funding formula.
sceneCN: 这里 legislation 指立法机关通过的法律（第 2 个义项：法规总称）；句意为议会通过了一项改写拨款公式的法律。

pos.zh: 一部法律（可数，常见于美式用法）

forms.label: 复数（指多部法律，多见于美式用法）

derivatives.zh: 立法（legislation 去后缀构成动词，由产物转指制定过程）
立法的（legislate + -ive「有……性质的」，由动作转指属性）
立法者；议员（legislate + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由动作转指机关）

senses.title: The making of laws
senses.definition: the process or act of making laws through an authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 由有权机关制定法律的过程或行为
senses.example: Legislation took eighteen months and three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 立法花了十八个月、经过三个委员会。
senses.why: the Latin noun names the bringing of a law, an act rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指「把法带来」，是行为而非物品。

senses.title: Laws collectively
senses.definition: the whole body of enacted laws on a subject or in a jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或某一法域已颁行的全部法律
senses.example: Environmental legislation now covers the whole watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 环境法规如今覆盖整个流域。
senses.why: mass-noun use treats statutes as one substance, which is how policy talk usually needs them.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把诸多法令当作一种物质，政策讨论通常正需要这样。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted law, countable especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一部已颁行的法律，在美式用法中可数
senses.example: Two legislations were merged into one act.
senses.exampleCN: 两部法令被合并为一项法案。
senses.why: American usage makes the noun countable because each bill becomes a numbered law.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个名词可数化，因为每项议案都会成为一部编号法律。

senses.title: The legislative process
senses.definition: the staged procedure of reading, amending and voting that a bill must pass
senses.definitionCN: 议案必须经过的宣读、修正与表决的分阶段程序
senses.example: The rules of legislation favour whoever controls the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 立法程序偏向掌控议程的一方。
senses.why: procedure is the machinery behind the act, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 程序是行为背后的机器，英语用同一个名词兼指两者。

senses.title: What a legislature enacts
senses.definition: the output of a parliament or congress, as distinct from rules made by agencies
senses.definitionCN: 议会或国会的产出，区别于行政机关自订的规则
senses.example: Primary legislation needs a vote; guidance does not.
senses.exampleCN: 主要立法需要表决，行政指引则不必。
senses.why: the word marks the source of authority, so it separates parliamentary output from administrative rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示权威来源，因此把议会产出与行政规则分开。

senses.title: Delegated legislation
senses.definition: rules made by a minister or agency under powers granted by a statute
senses.definitionCN: 部长或机关依法律授予的权力制定的规则
senses.example: Delegated legislation fills in technical detail the chamber cannot debate.
senses.exampleCN: 次级立法填补议会无法逐条辩论的技术细节。
senses.why: the word travels with the authority to make law, even when that authority has been lent out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随立法权一同转移，即使该权力是被借出去的。

senses.title: Proposed legislation
senses.definition: a bill or draft still before the chamber, spoken of as future law
senses.definitionCN: 仍在议会审议、被视作未来法律的议案或草案
senses.example: Proposed legislation would cap the fee at ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 拟议立法将把这个费用上限设为百分之十。
senses.why: the word is applied ahead of enactment because the shape of the law is already visible in the draft.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在通过之前就被使用，因为法律的形状在草案里已经可见。

senses.title: Rules for an organization
senses.titleCN: 引申：组织内部规则体系
senses.definition: the formal rules by which a body governs its own members or processes
senses.definitionCN: 某机构管理自身成员或流程的成文规则
senses.example: The society's legislation on conflicts of interest is three pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会关于利益冲突的规则有三页纸。
senses.why: private bodies borrow the word when their rules begin to function like statutes.
senses.whyCN: 私人机构在其规则开始像法令一样运作时，便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Legislation comes from Latin legis latio 'a bringing of a law', from lex 'law' and latio 'a bringing', the noun of latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislation 来自拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」，由 lex「法」与 latio「带来」构成，后者是 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus 的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex meant 'law, statute, a motion put to the people'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为「法、法令、提交民众的动议」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bring' has the suppletive participle latus, from which latio 'a bringing' is formed; the two verbs were already fused in classical usage.
items.cn: ferre「搬运、带来」的过去分词为异干互补的 latus，由其构成 latio「带来」；两者在古典用法中已合并。

items.en: The phrase legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly, a procedural act rather than the text itself.
items.cn: legis latio 这一说法指把议案带到大会之前的程序性行为，而非文本本身。

items.en: Medieval Latin legislatio generalized the phrase into the making of laws by any authorized body.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 legislatio 把这一说法一般化，指任何有权机关制定法律。

items.en: French législation passed into English in the seventeenth century, first as the act and soon after as the body of laws.
items.cn: 法语 législation 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指立法行为，不久也指法律总体。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the origin of lex itself remains unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 本身的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the lex or legisl- stem; group two holds words for laws and for the making of them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 lex 或 legisl- 词干；第二组是关于法律与制定法律的词。

entries.definition: Describing a body or power that makes law; it cannot stand for the laws themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 描述制定法律的机关或权力；不能指法律本身。

entries.definition: The assembly that makes law, formed with -ure 'place or body'; a different thing from the laws it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的议会，由 -ure「场所、机构」构成；与其所制定的法律是两回事。

entries.definition: One member who makes law; the noun names a role, not an output.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员之一；指角色，而非产出。

entries.definition: From Latin legitimus 'lawful', built on lex but through a different adjective; it means lawful, not law-making.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legitimus「合法的」，虽出 lex 却经另一形容词；意为合法，而非立法。

entries.definition: A single rule or the whole body of rules; legislation is the making of it or the output as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 单条规则或全部规则；legislation 指制定过程或作为总体的产出。

entries.definition: A single law passed by a legislature, countable and technical; legislation is the wider mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的单项法律，可数且技术化；legislation 是更宽的总称。

entries.definition: Detailed rules issued by an agency under a statute, usually not requiring a parliamentary vote.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的细则，通常不经议会表决。

entries.definition: A draft law still under consideration; legislation names what it becomes, or the process of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在审议的草案；legislation 指它最终成为的东西，或制定它的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio: the bringing of a law, so the word began as a motion carried forward.
normal.cn: legis latio：把法带来，因此这个词本是一项被送上前的动议。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split act from output: pass legislation, delegated legislation, environmental legislation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出行为与产出：通过立法、授权立法、环境立法。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: a bill is the draft, legislation is the making and the mass of laws.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bill 是草案，legislation 是制定过程与法律总体。

normal.en: Watch the false friend legitimate: lawful, but built on a different adjective of lex.
normal.cn: 提防假朋友 legitimate：意为合法，却由 lex 的另一形容词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a text carried by hand across a hall before anyone votes on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文本在被人手捧着穿过大厅，之后才有人表决。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that grow a new thick volume every session.
abstract.cn: 想象书架每开一次会就多一本厚册。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that must be read aloud before it can bind anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则必须先被大声读出，才能约束任何人。

examples.en: The state's legislation on groundwater is older than its mapping.
examples.cn: 该州关于地下水的立法比水文测绘还要早。

examples.en: Delegated legislation filled in the standards the chamber left blank.
examples.cn: 次级立法填上了议会留白的技术标准。

examples.en: Industry lobbied against the proposed legislation for two years.
examples.cn: 业界游说反对这项拟议立法达两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lation（带来）＝ 把法带到台面上；记「念一遍、改一遍、举一次手」。

root: 拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」= lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latio「带来」（来自 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a bill from act to archive: making law, the mass of law, one statute, the procedure, parliamentary output, delegated rules, drafts not yet passed, and the rules of a private body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一项议案从行为走到档案：立法、法律总体、单部法律、程序、议会产出、授权规则、尚未通过的草案，以及私人机构的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a text read aloud, amended, voted on, then bound into a thick volume.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文本被朗读、修正、表决，最后装订进厚册。

branches.en: ACT AND MASS: the making of law, then the whole body it accumulates into.
branches.cn: 行为与总体：先制定，再累积成整体。

branches.en: ONE VOLUME: the countable unit inside the mass.
branches.cn: 单册：总体之中的可数单位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: procedure at work, and the authority that makes its output law.
branches.cn: 机器：程序在运转，以及使其产成为法律的权威。

branches.en: LENT POWER: rule-making handed to ministers and agencies.
branches.cn: 借出的权力：规则制定权交到部长与机关手里。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER THE HALL: drafts spoken of as law, and private bodies drafting their own.
branches.cn: 大厅前后：草案已被当作法律谈论，私人机构也自订规则。

intro.en: Legislation joins a Latin noun for law to a Latin noun for bringing, and the second element still appears in English words of transfer.
intro.cn: legislation 把拉丁语「法」的名词与「带来」的名词接在一起，后一成分仍出现在英语的转移类词中。

latinIntro.en: Lex supplies legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre supply transfer, refer and relate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate。

items.example: Lex is the root of legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: lex 是 legal 与 legislate 的词根。

items.example: Its participle latus hides inside latio.
items.exampleCN: 其分词 latus 藏在 latio 里。

items.example: Legis latio is the bringing of a bill.
items.exampleCN: legis latio 就是把议案带来。

items.example: The chamber legislates twice a year.
Legislation followed the report by a year.
items.exampleCN: 报告之后一年才有了立法。

items.example: The legislator read the amendment aloud.
items.exampleCN: 立法者大声读了修正案。

items.example: A legitimate claim differs from a popular one.
items.exampleCN: 合法的诉求与受欢迎的诉求不同。

definition_zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动；悠闲；休闲（作定语）
definition_en: time free from work or duties, the activities that fill it, and the relaxed manner that such time allows
core_image: 安静午后的一张空藤椅，旁边放着一杯还冒着热气的茶
scene: 周末的午后，会议与邮件都停了，阳台上的藤椅空着，等一个人端着茶坐下来。Long afternoons of leisure left him free to read whatever he liked.
sceneCN: 这里是「空闲时间」（第 1 个义项：不必工作的自由时间）；句意为漫长的闲暇午后让他能随心读书。图中可辨识物件：阳台藤椅、茶杯、翻开的书。

pos.zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动

derivatives.zh: 由 leisure 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「从容的；不慌不忙的」
由 leisure 加 -ed 构成，义为「有大量空闲时间的」
由 leisure 与 wear 复合而成，义为「休闲服饰」

senses.title: Time free from work or duty
senses.definition: time when you are not working and may choose for yourself what to do
senses.definitionCN: 不必工作、可以由自己决定做什么的那段时间
senses.example: She has little leisure during the exam season.
senses.exampleCN: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。
senses.why: Latin licere meant to be permitted, so leisure began as permitted time, the hours no duty can claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licere 意为「被允许」，leisure 最初指被允许自由支配的时间，也就是没有职责占用的那几个小时。

senses.title: Activities enjoyed in that free time
senses.definition: the things people choose to do for pleasure when work is finished
senses.definitionCN: 工作结束后人们为了愉快而选择去做的事情
senses.example: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。
senses.why: Once free hours exist they must be filled, so the word slides from the empty time to the chosen activity that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 空闲的小时一旦存在，就必然被填满，于是词义从「空白的时间」滑向占用这段时间的自选活动。

senses.title: An unhurried, easy manner
senses.definition: a relaxed way of acting, with no pressure of time and no need to rush
senses.definitionCN: 不受时间压迫、不必赶的轻松做事方式
senses.example: He answered the questions at his leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。
senses.why: Time that carries no deadline produces a manner without hurry, so at leisure comes to describe the calm inside the free hours.
senses.whyCN: 没有截止期限的时间会带来不赶的态度，于是 at leisure 用来描述空闲时间里那种从容的心境。

senses.title: Placed before a noun: made for free time
senses.definition: used in front of another noun for places, clothes or industries serving people at leisure
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，指服务于闲暇之人的场所、衣物或产业
senses.example: The town opened a new leisure centre last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇去年春天新开了一家休闲中心。
senses.why: A noun naming free time easily turns into a label on the things built for it, which is why leisure attaches to centres, wear and whole industries.
senses.whyCN: 表示空闲时间的名词很容易变成「为其建造之物」的标签，所以 leisure 能贴在中心、服饰乃至整个产业前面。

intro.en: Leisure comes from a Latin verb of permission and reached English through French, still carrying the idea of hours that nobody else can claim.
intro.cn: leisure 源自拉丁语中表示「允许」的动词，经法语进入英语，至今仍带着「无人能占用的时间」这层意思。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or permitted, and it named what a person was free to do.
items.cn: licere 意为「被允许、获准」，指一个人可以自由去做的事。

items.en: Its noun licentia named permission or freedom, the state of being allowed.
items.cn: 其名词 licentia 表示许可或自由，即「获准的状态」。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as leisir, which meant both to be allowed and the free time that followed.
items.cn: 古法语把动词写作 leisir，既表示「被允许」，也指随之而来的空闲时间。

items.en: Middle English used leisir, later spelled leisure, for time at one's own disposal.
items.cn: 中古英语用 leisir（后写作 leisure）指由自己支配的时间。

items.en: Modern English keeps leisure for free time and extends it to leisure activities, leisure wear and the leisure industry.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leisure 指空闲时间，并扩展到休闲活动、休闲服饰与休闲产业。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin verb of permission; the near-meaning group collects words for spare hours and rest.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「允许」动词上的派生形式；近义组收表示空闲与休息的词。

entries.definition: Acting or moving without hurry.
entries.definitionCN: 不慌不忙的；从容的。

entries.definition: Having plenty of free time, usually through wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 有大量空闲时间的，通常因富裕。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; the opposite of illicit.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；illicit 的反义词。

entries.definition: Official permission to do something, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 官方许可，来自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Time left over after work or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 工作或职责之外剩下的时间。

entries.definition: Resting and letting tension go.
entries.definitionCN: 休息，让紧张消退。

entries.definition: Activities done for enjoyment outside work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作之外为消遣而做的活动。

entries.definition: The state of not working, often with a hint of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不做事的状态，常带一点贬义。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for being allowed, and its family keeps returning to permission, free hours and the easy manner they produce.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「获准」的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到许可、空闲时间以及由此产生的从容态度。

normal.en: Licere in Latin means to be allowed, so leisure is time you are permitted to spend as you wish.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 licere 意为被允许，所以 leisure 是可以随自己支配的获准时间。

normal.en: Old French leisir dropped its verb ending and became leisure, keeping both the permission and the free hours.
normal.cn: 古法语 leisir 去掉动词词尾后成为 leisure，同时保留「许可」和「空闲时间」两层意思。

normal.en: Leisurely adds -ly to leisure, describing the unhurried manner of someone inside free time.
normal.cn: leisurely 在 leisure 后加 -ly，形容人处在空闲时间里的从容样子。

normal.en: Leisure wear joins leisure to wear, clothing for hours when no uniform is required.
normal.cn: leisure wear 把 leisure 与 wear 连起来，指不必穿制服的时段所穿的衣服。

normal.en: The phrase is at leisure, not in leisure, because you sit inside your own free time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 at leisure 而不是 in leisure，因为人坐在自己的空闲时间里。

abstract.en: A word that first meant permission reminds us that free time is not empty space but time granted to us.
abstract.cn: 一个最初表示「许可」的词提醒人：空闲不是空白，而是被准许使用的时光。

abstract.en: Leisure links restful hours with a calm manner, suggesting that how we spend time shapes how we carry ourselves.
abstract.cn: leisure 把休息的时段与从容的态度连在一起，说明怎样花时间会影响人的举止。

abstract.en: When leisure becomes an industry, the very hours once free now have goods built around them.
abstract.cn: 当 leisure 变成一种产业，原本自由的时段周围就长出了专门为它制造的商品。

examples.en: She has little leisure during the exam season.
examples.cn: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。

examples.en: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
examples.cn: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。

examples.en: He answered the questions at his leisure.
examples.cn: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来这儿」——有空的时候，来这儿坐坐；记住 leisure 是空闲、闲暇。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ 拉丁名词 licentia（许可）→ 古法语 leisir（获准的空闲）→ 中古英语 leisure；同族词多与「许可、自由」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is permitted free time; from it grow the activities that fill those hours, the unhurried manner they allow, and the attributive use for things made for them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被允许自由支配的时间」；由此长出填充这些时间的活动、随之而来的从容态度，以及修饰休闲事物的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair on a quiet afternoon, waiting for someone with nowhere else to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静午后的一张空椅子，等一个无别处可去的人。

branches.en: a clock with no appointment marked on it
branches.cn: 一只没有记下任何约会的钟

branches.en: a bicycle leaning against a park bench
branches.cn: 靠在公园长椅上的自行车

branches.en: a town building named after free hours

definition_zh: 借出；出借；放贷；提供（帮助）；适宜于
definition_en: to give something to someone for a time, to supply money on credit, and to hand over help, attention or a quality
core_image: 一只手把伞递出去，另一只手空着，等伞回来
scene: 雨天教室门口，一个人把伞递过去，自己缩起肩膀跑进雨里。He lent her his umbrella and walked home wet.
sceneCN: 这里是「借出」（第 1 个义项：把东西暂时交给别人用）；句意是他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。图中可辨识物件：雨伞、雨滴、教室门框。

pos.zh: 借出；出借；放贷；提供；适宜于

derivatives.zh: 由 lend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「出借人；放贷方」
由 lend 加 -ing 构成，义为「出借；放贷业务」
由 lend 加 -able 构成，义为「可出借的」

senses.title: To give something for a limited time
senses.titleCN: 借出（把东西暂时给别人用）
senses.definition: to give an object to someone on the understanding that it will come back later
senses.definitionCN: 把某物交给别人，双方都明白以后要归还
senses.example: He lent her his umbrella and walked home wet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。
senses.why: The old verb means granting the use of a thing rather than giving it away, so the object is expected to return and the owner keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 这个古词本义是「准许别人使用」，而不是「送出去」，所以东西预期会回来，主人始终保有它。

senses.title: To supply money that must be repaid
senses.definition: to give money to a person or business for a period, usually with interest
senses.definitionCN: 把钱在一段时间内交给个人或企业，通常收取利息
senses.example: The bank lends money to small firms at a fixed rate.
senses.exampleCN: 银行按固定利率向小公司放贷。
senses.why: Money is the thing most often granted for a period, so the general verb of temporary giving becomes the standard word for credit.
senses.whyCN: 钱是最常被「限期交付」的东西，于是这个表示暂时给予的通用动词成了「信贷」的标准说法。

senses.title: To be suitable for a particular use
senses.definition: to have qualities that make something easy or fitting to do
senses.definitionCN: 具备某些性质，使某件事做起来合适或容易
senses.example: The quiet garden lends itself to long conversations.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园很适合长谈。
senses.why: English says a place lends itself to a purpose, as if it handed its own qualities over for a while, which is why suitability comes out of the lending image.
senses.whyCN: 英语说某地「把自己借给」某种用途，仿佛它把自己的性质暂时交出来，所以「适合」这层意思是从借出的形象里长出来的。

senses.title: To offer help, attention or support
senses.definition: to give help, an ear or support to someone for as long as it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 在别人需要时给予帮助、倾听或支持
senses.example: She lent an ear to every student who needed one.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是需要倾诉的学生，她都愿意听。
senses.why: Help and attention can be handed over for a while without being owned, so the same verb covers listening, backing and encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 帮助与关注可以暂时交付而不必归对方所有，所以同一个动词也能覆盖倾听、支持与鼓励。

intro.en: Lend is a native Germanic verb, twin to the noun loan, and its irregular past lent keeps an old English shape.
intro.cn: lend 是土生土长的日耳曼语动词，与名词 loan 同出一源，不规则过去式 lent 保留了古英语的形态。

items.en: A reconstructed root laihwan meant to lend, or to leave something with someone for a time.
items.cn: 重构词根 laihwan 意为借出，或把东西暂时留在别人手里。

items.en: Old English lǣnan meant to grant the use of something, and the related noun lǣn meant a loan.
items.cn: 古英语 lǣnan 意为准许别人使用某物，相关名词 lǣn 意为借出物。

items.en: Norse speakers used a related verb, and their forms reinforced the English word in the north of England.
items.cn: 北欧使用者有相关动词，其形式在英格兰北部强化了英语这个词。

items.en: Middle English lenen kept the short past form lent, which survived into modern use.
items.cn: 中古英语 lenen 保留了短过去式 lent，并一直沿用到现代。

items.en: Modern English keeps lend as the verb and loan as the noun, with lent serving as both past tense and past participle.
items.cn: 现代英语让 lend 固定为动词、loan 作名词，lent 同时充当过去式与过去分词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun twin and two forms built with English suffixes; the near-meaning group collects words for borrowing, credit and money advanced.
note.cn: 形近组收同源名词与两个用英语后缀构成的派生形式；近义组收表示借入、信贷与垫付的词。

entries.definitionCN: lend 的同源名词，指被借出的东西或款项。

entries.definition: A person or bank that lends.
entries.definitionCN: 出借人或放贷机构。

entries.definition: The act or business of lending money.

entries.definition: To take something for a time and agree to return it.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时拿走某物并同意归还，方向与 lend 相反。

entries.definition: To pay money before it is due, or to lend it.
entries.definitionCN: 提前支付或在到期前垫付。

entries.definition: Permission to pay later for goods or money received.
entries.definitionCN: 先收货或收款、以后付款的许可。

entries.definition: To give something formally, often a right or a favour.
entries.definitionCN: 正式给予，多指权利或恩惠。

normalIntro.en: The word is a native Germanic verb whose noun twin is loan, and its family keeps returning to temporary giving and the trust that makes it possible.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是土生土长的日耳曼语动词，同源名词是 loan，同族词反复回到「暂时给予」以及让这种给予成为可能的信任。

normal.en: Lend and loan are twins from the same root: the verb lends, the noun is the loan.
normal.cn: lend 与 loan 同出一源：动词是 lend，借出的东西是 loan。

normal.en: The past tense is lent, not lended, because the old strong shape survived while most verbs became regular.
normal.cn: 过去式是 lent 而不是 lended，因为古老的强变化形态留了下来，而多数动词都变成了规则变化。

normal.en: Lender adds -er to lend: the person or bank on the giving side.
normal.cn: lender 在 lend 后加 -er，指出借的一方，可以是人，也可以是银行。

normal.en: Lending adds -ing and turns the act into a business, as in bank lending.
normal.cn: lending 加 -ing，把行为变成一门业务，如银行放贷。

normal.en: Lend itself to is fixed: the thing lends itself, never lends to itself, when it suits a use.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 lend itself to：表示适合某种用途时，用反身形式，不能省掉 itself。

abstract.en: A word for handing something over temporarily is also a word for trust, since every loan assumes the other person will return it.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「暂时交出」的词同时也是「信任」的词，因为每一次出借都预设对方会归还。

abstract.en: Lending a hand and lending money share one verb, which quietly ranks money and help as similar kinds of gift.
abstract.cn: 借出一只手和借出钱共用一个动词，这悄悄把钱与帮助归为同一类给予。

abstract.en: The fact that a garden can lend itself to talk shows how English turns an act of giving into a statement about fitness.
abstract.cn: 花园能「把自己借给」谈话，说明英语能把一个给予动作变成关于「合不合适」的判断。

examples.cn: 他把伞借给她，自己淋着雨回家。

examples.cn: 银行按固定利率向小公司放贷。

examples.cn: 安静的花园很适合长谈。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「暂时给予」；义项由此分出有息借贷的钱、交付出去的帮助与关注，以及表示「适合某用途」的反身用法。

definition_zh: 长度；长度单位；时长；程度；一段
definition_en: the measurement of something from end to end, its duration in time, the extent to which something is carried out, and a piece cut from something long
core_image: 卷尺从墙角拉到另一头，刻度停在木板的边缘
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉到墙角，低头看刻度，然后在木板上画下一道线。He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
sceneCN: 这里是「长度」（第 1 个义项：从一端到另一端的量）；句意是他在裁板之前先量了桌子的长度。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、铅笔与墙角。

derivatives.zh: 由 length 加 -y 构成，义为「冗长的；漫长的」
由 length 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加长；变长」
由 length 与 wise 复合而成，义为「纵向地；沿长度方向」

senses.title: The measurement from end to end
senses.definition: the distance measured along something from one end to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沿某物从一端量到另一端的距离
senses.example: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。
senses.why: Old English lengþu was built from lang plus a suffix of abstract nouns, so the word names the quality a thing has by being long.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lengþu 由 lang（长）加抽象名词后缀构成，所以这个词指的就是事物「长」这一性质。

senses.title: The amount of time something lasts
senses.definition: the period during which something continues from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 某件事从开始到结束所持续的时间
senses.example: The length of the film surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line with two ends, so the same word for spatial extent is borrowed to measure how long an event runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条有两端的线，于是表示空间延展的同一个词被借来量一件事持续多久。

senses.title: The extent to which something is done
senses.definition: how fully or how far an action, argument or piece of writing is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 行动、论述或文章做到多完整、多深入
senses.example: The report discussed the causes at length.
senses.exampleCN: 报告详细讨论了各种原因。
senses.why: Just as a physical thing has a measurable extent, an argument can be carried to a certain extent, which gives the phrase at length its sense of full treatment.
senses.whyCN: 正如实物有可量的延展，一段论述也能被推进到某个「长度」，于是 at length 就有了「充分论述」的意思。

senses.title: A piece cut from something long
senses.definition: a measured piece of rope, pipe or cloth taken from a longer whole
senses.definitionCN: 从更长的整根绳、管或布上截下来的一段
senses.example: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
senses.exampleCN: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。
senses.why: Once length names a measurable extent, a piece that has exactly that extent can itself be called a length, especially in rope and timber.
senses.whyCN: 既然 length 表示可量的长度，那么恰好具有这个长度的一段东西也就能被称为 a length，绳索与木料尤其如此。

intro.en: Length is the oldest English way of naming the quality of being long, formed from the adjective long with a suffix that builds abstract nouns.
intro.cn: length 是英语里指「长」这一性质最古老的说法，由形容词 long 加上构成抽象名词的后缀而来。

items.en: A reconstructed form dlonghos underlies the family of long words, and the same root appears in Latin longus, which is why the two branches look alike.
items.cn: 重构形式 dlonghos 是这一族「长」词的共同来源，同一词根也出现在拉丁语 longus，因此两条分支看起来相似。

items.en: Old English lang meant long in space and in time, and it could also describe a tall person.
items.cn: 古英语 lang 既指空间上的长，也指时间上的长，还能形容人个子高。

items.en: Adding the abstract suffix -þu to lang produced lengþu, the state or measure of being long.
items.cn: 在 lang 后加抽象名词后缀 -þu 得到 lengþu，即「长」的状态或量。

items.en: Middle English respelled the word with th and dropped the old ending, arriving at forms like lengthe.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写改成 th 并丢掉旧词尾，出现了 lengthe 这样的形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on length, kept lengths as its plural, and extended the sense to duration and to a measured piece.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 length，复数 lengths，并把词义扩展到时长与截下的一段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjectives and verbs built on the same long root; the near-meaning group collects words for measured extent and time span.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「长」词根上的形容词与动词；近义组收表示量度延展与时间跨度的词。

entries.definition: Lasting too long or taking more time than needed.
entries.definitionCN: 持续过久或比需要的更费时的。

entries.definition: To make something longer or to become longer.
entries.definitionCN: 使变长；变长。

entries.definition: The adjective from which length was built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 length 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: Distance east or west on the earth, from the Latin word for length.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的东西距离，来自拉丁语中表示「长度」的词。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间。

entries.definition: The time during which something continues.
entries.definitionCN: 某事持续的时间。

entries.definition: The degree to which something reaches or is true.
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或真实程度。

entries.definition: The full distance or period from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的全部距离或时段。

normalIntro.en: The word is the abstract noun of long, and its family keeps returning to measurement in space, measurement in time and the extent of an action.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 long 的抽象名词，同族词反复回到空间上的量、时间上的量，以及行动的推进程度。

normal.en: Length is long turned into a noun: if a thing is long, its length is the measure of that.
normal.cn: length 是把 long 变成名词：一个东西「长」，它的 length 就是这份长的量。

normal.en: The plural is lengths with th kept, not lengthths, so the spelling adds only an s after the th.
normal.cn: 复数是 lengths，th 保留不动，只在 th 后加 s。

normal.en: Lengthen adds -en to length and turns the measure back into an action of making longer.
normal.cn: lengthen 在 length 后加 -en，把「量」又变回「使之变长」的动作。

normal.en: Lengthy adds -y but carries a hint of criticism: more length than the situation needs.
normal.cn: lengthy 加 -y，却带一点批评意味：长度超过了场合所需。

normal.en: At length means two things at once: after a long time, and in full detail.
normal.cn: at length 同时有两个意思：经过很长时间之后，以及详细地。

abstract.en: The same word measures a table, a film and an argument, which shows how readily English maps time and reasoning onto space.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能量桌子、量影片、量论述，说明英语很自然地把时间和论证都投射到空间上。

abstract.en: A measured piece of rope is called a length, so the abstract measure becomes a concrete object when a knife cuts it.
abstract.cn: 截下的一段绳子也叫 a length，于是抽象的量在刀落下时变成了具体的物。

abstract.en: Long is the adjective of desire and length is its measure, but lengthy is the word we use when the desire has gone on too long.
abstract.cn: long 是表示渴望的形容词，length 是它的度量，而 lengthy 用在「拖得太久」的时候。

examples.en: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
examples.cn: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。

examples.en: The length of the film surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「愣是」——这根绳子愣是有三米长；记住 length 是长度。

root: 原始印欧语重构形式 dlonghos（长）→ 古英语 lang → 加抽象后缀 -þu 成 lengþu → 中古英语 lengthe → 现代英语 length；与拉丁语 longus 同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the measure of being long; the senses then apply that measure to time, to how far an action is carried, and to a piece cut to that size.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「长」的量；义项再把这个量用到时间上、用到行动推进的程度上，以及用到恰好截成那么长的一段东西上。

core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺从墙角一直拉到木板的另一头。

branches.cn: 沿木板铺开的卷尺

branches.cn: 标出一部两小时影片的钟面

branches.cn: 一页页慢慢读完的报告

intro.en: The word joins the adjective long to an Old English suffix for abstract nouns, and the family then adds endings for quality, action and direction.
intro.cn: 这个词把形容词 long 与古英语的抽象名词后缀接在一起，同族词再加上表示性质、动作与方向的词尾。

definition_zh: 较少的；更少的；较少地；不如……的
definition_en: smaller in amount or degree than something else; to a smaller extent; also used before an adjective to mean not at all
core_image: 同一只杯子里，水线比刚才低了一截
scene: 妈妈把壶里的水倒进两个杯子，又往其中一个补了半杯，先递给孩子的那只明显装得更少。The second cup held far less than the first, so the child drank it in one gulp.
sceneCN: 这里是「较少的、更少量的」（第 1 个义项：用于不可数名词，表示分量比另一物小）；句意为第二杯比第一杯少得多，孩子一口就喝完了。图中可辨识物件：水壶、两只杯子、低下去的水线。

senses.title: A smaller amount of something
senses.definition: a smaller amount of something, used mainly with uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 某物的分量比另一物小，主要与不可数名词连用
senses.example: Add less sugar next time.
senses.exampleCN: 下次少放点糖。
senses.why: Less began as the comparative of little, so its base picture is one pile measured against another and found shorter.
senses.whyCN: less 原本是 little 的比较级，因此它的底层画面是两堆东西放在一起量，其中一堆明显更矮。

senses.title: A smaller number of people or things
senses.definition: a smaller number of people or things than another group
senses.definitionCN: 人或物的数目比另一组小，口语中常用于可数名词复数
senses.example: The new hall holds less people than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新礼堂装的人比旧礼堂少。
senses.why: Once the word means a shorter measure, English speakers extend it from stuff that is measured to people who are counted, even though strict grammar prefers fewer.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「量更短」，说话人便会把它从可以量的东西扩展到可以数的人，尽管严格语法更倾向用 fewer。

senses.title: To a smaller degree
senses.definition: to a smaller degree, extent or frequency than before or than another
senses.definitionCN: 程度、范围或频率比原先或比另一者更小
senses.example: She works less in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天她干活少一些。
senses.why: The same comparison moves from quantity to degree: not a smaller pile, but a smaller share of effort, time or attention.
senses.whyCN: 同样的比较从数量转到程度：不再是更小的一堆，而是在力气、时间或注意力上占更小的份额。

senses.title: Not at all, far from
senses.titleCN: 远非；一点也不（用于 less than + 形容词）
senses.definition: used in the phrase less than before an adjective to mean hardly or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 用于 less than 加形容词的结构，表示几乎不、根本算不上
senses.example: His answer was less than polite.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答可算不上客气。
senses.why: If something falls short of a standard by an unknown amount, the comparison becomes a polite way of saying it fails the standard entirely.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物离某个标准差着一截而不知差多少，这种比较就变成一种客气的说法，实际意思是它根本没达到标准。

intro.en: Less is a shortened form of a much older comparative word, and it has kept the job of measuring one thing against another ever since.
intro.cn: less 是一个更古老的比较级词缩略而来的，自那以后一直承担着把一物与另一物放在一起衡量的任务。

items.en: A root reconstructed as les- is thought to have carried the idea of smallness or slenderness, though the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 les-，带有「小、细」的意思，但这一构拟并不确定。

items.en: Old English had the comparative lǣssa and the adverb lǣs, both meaning a smaller amount, and the forms were already irregular.
items.cn: 古英语已有比较级 lǣssa 和副词 lǣs，都表示「更少的量」，而且这些形式早就不规则。

items.en: Middle English shortened the word to lesse, dropped the final vowel, and used it both for amount and for degree.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短为 lesse，又脱落了词尾元音，并用它同时表示分量与程度。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries fixed less as the comparative of little in print, beside least as its superlative.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者在印刷文本中把 less 固定为 little 的比较级，与最高级 least 配对。

items.en: Modern usage keeps less for uncountable nouns, allows it informally with plurals, and adds fixed phrases such as less than and more or less.
items.cn: 现代用法让 less 主要修饰不可数名词，口语中容许它接复数，并发展出 less than、more or less 等固定短语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same comparative stem; the near-meaning group collects words that measure a falling amount.
note.cn: 形近组收同一比较级词干上的词；近义组收表示「数量变少」的词。

entries.definition: The superlative of little, naming the smallest amount of all.
entries.definitionCN: little 的最高级，指所有当中最小的量。

entries.definition: Smaller or less important when two things are compared.
entries.definitionCN: 两者相比时较小或较次要的。

entries.definition: To become or make something smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 变小；使减少。

entries.definition: A conjunction meaning if not, formed from less in the sense of a smaller condition; the spelling is close but the grammar is separate.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「除非」的连词，由表示「少一些条件」的 less 参与构成，拼写相近但语法作用不同。

entries.definition: A smaller number of countable things, the strict partner of less.
entries.definitionCN: 可数事物的数目更少，是与 less 严格对应的说法。

entries.definition: Of less size, used of physical things rather than amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸更小，多用于具体物体而不是数量。

entries.definition: Smaller in level, price or rank rather than in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平、价格或等级更低，而不是数量更少。

normalIntro.en: The word is a comparative that keeps two piles in view at once, so every memory hook should compare something with something else.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是比较级，画面里始终有两堆东西，所以每条记忆钩子都要把一物与另一物放在一起比。

normal.en: Less is the comparative of little: little, less, least is the irregular ladder to climb.
normal.cn: less 是 little 的比较级：little、less、least 构成一条不规则的三级阶梯。

normal.en: The ending -er signals comparison, which is why less never takes a second -er.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 本身就是比较级的标志，所以 less 后面不能再加一个 -er。

normal.en: Less pairs with uncountable nouns such as water, money and time, while fewer pairs with things you can count.
normal.cn: less 与 water、money、time 这类不可数名词搭配，fewer 则与可以数的东西搭配。

normal.en: Lessen is less plus the verb ending -en, so to lessen is to make the smaller amount happen.
normal.cn: lessen 是 less 加动词词尾 -en，所以 lessen 就是「让更小的量发生」，即减少。

normal.en: Less than before an adjective, as in less than honest, means the quality is absent rather than merely weak.
normal.cn: less than 放在形容词前，如 less than honest，表示这种品质根本不存在，而不只是弱一点。

abstract.en: Two piles side by side are the oldest picture of comparison, and less is the shorter pile named in one syllable.
abstract.cn: 两堆东西并排，是最古老的比较画面，而 less 就是一个音节说出的那堆更矮的。

abstract.en: A word that measures downwards is useful because English likes to compare before it describes.
abstract.cn: 一个专门往低处量的词很有用，因为英语习惯先比较，再描述。

abstract.en: When less than turns polite, the comparison stops measuring and starts judging.
abstract.cn: 当 less than 变得客气，比较就不再是量多少，而是在下判断。

examples.en: Try to spend less time on your phone.
examples.cn: 试着少花点时间在手机上。

examples.en: The trip took less than two hours.
examples.cn: 这趟行程用了不到两个小时。

examples.en: He was less than happy about the delay.
examples.cn: 他对这次延误可不太高兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累死」——活儿干得多就累死，干得少就不累；less 是更少。

root: 一般认为源自一个表示「小、细」的重构词根 les-，古英语作 lǣssa（比较级）、lǣs（副词），中古英语缩为 lesse，再变为 less。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a shorter measure; from there the word reaches amounts, then countable groups, then degree, and finally the judgment hidden in less than.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「量得更短」；由此依次扩展到分量、可数群体、程度，最后是藏在 less than 里的评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the water line in the same cup sitting lower than before.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只杯子里的水线，比刚才低了一截。

branches.en: a cup filled only halfway
branches.cn: 只倒了一半的杯子

branches.en: a hall with empty seats at the back
branches.cn: 后排空着座位的礼堂

branches.en: a shorter working day in winter
branches.cn: 冬天更短的工作日

branches.en: a reply that fails to be polite
branches.cn: 一句谈不上客气的回答

branches.en: two piles measured against each other
branches.cn: 两堆东西放在一起比高低

intro.en: The word is held up by the irregular comparative ladder of little and by two English suffixes that turn the stem into a quality, a verb and a fixed compound.
intro.cn: 这个词由 little 的不规则比较级阶梯，以及两个把词干变成性质、动词和固定复合词的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 课；一节课；课文；教训；告诫；圣经选读
definition_en: a period of teaching, a unit of study, an experience that teaches you something, a warning or rebuke, and a passage read in church
core_image: 黑板前站着的老师，把一段经文抄给台下低头记笔记的学生
scene: 午后教堂里只剩几个人，读经员翻到旧约的一页，用平稳的声音念出当天安排的那段经文。The old rector read the second lesson slowly, and the congregation answered at the end of each verse.
sceneCN: 这里是「（礼拜中诵读的）圣经选读」（第 5 个义项：教堂礼拜里指定朗读的一段经文）；句意为老牧师慢慢念出第二段选读，会众在每节末尾应和。图中可辨识物件：教堂长椅、摊开的旧约、读经台。

pos.zh: 课；课程单元；教训；告诫；圣经选读

collocations.zh: 第一课；礼拜中的第一段选读

derivatives.zh: 由 lesson 与 plan 复合而成，指教师课前写的教学方案
由 object 与 lesson 复合，原指用实物演示的课，后引申为可引以为戒的例子
由 lesson 的复数与 learned 构成的固定说法，指事后总结出的经验教训

senses.title: A period of teaching in a class
senses.definition: a period of time in which someone is taught a subject, especially in a school
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内有人教授某门科目，尤指学校里的课时
senses.example: Our first lesson starts at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的第一节课八点开始。
senses.why: The word came through French from a Latin verb meaning to read, so a lesson was first the text read aloud, then the time set aside for reading it with a teacher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自一个意为「读」的拉丁动词，所以 lesson 最初指朗读的文本，再指留出来跟老师一起读它的那段时间。

senses.title: A unit of study in a book or course
senses.definition: a section of a book or course that teaches one topic
senses.definitionCN: 书或课程中讲解一个主题的一个单元
senses.example: Lesson three is about weather.
senses.exampleCN: 第三课讲天气。
senses.why: Once a lesson is the reading assigned, the same word naturally names the chapter that holds that reading and the exercises built on it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 lesson 指布置下来要读的那段文字，同一个词自然也能指包含这段文字和配套练习的章节。

senses.title: An experience that teaches you something
senses.definition: an experience from which you learn how to act better in the future
senses.definitionCN: 一段让人学到以后该怎么做得更好的经历
senses.example: The flood taught the town a hard lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水给小镇上了沉重的一课。
senses.why: What is read and studied becomes what life forces you to learn, so the classroom word spreads to any experience that leaves knowledge behind.
senses.whyCN: 被读到、被学习的东西，会变成生活强迫你学会的东西，于是课堂上的词扩展到任何留下知识的经历。

senses.title: A warning or rebuke meant to correct someone
senses.definition: a warning, scolding or punishment given so that someone stops behaving badly
senses.definitionCN: 为了让某人不再犯错而给的警告、斥责或惩罚
senses.example: The coach made him run extra laps to teach him a lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让他多跑几圈，好给他一个教训。
senses.why: A lesson that is never forgotten usually hurts a little, so the word also names the sharp reminder that pain delivers on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一节忘不掉的课通常带点疼，于是这个词也指那种故意用疼痛给出的尖锐提醒。

senses.title: A passage read aloud in a church service
senses.definition: a passage from the Bible read aloud during a church service
senses.definitionCN: 教堂礼拜中当众朗读的一段圣经经文
senses.example: The reading of the lesson came after the opening hymn.
senses.exampleCN: 开场的赞美诗之后是圣经选读。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of all: in church the lesson is simply the passage that the reader reads out, long before the word entered the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是最古老的一个义项：在教堂里，lesson 就是读经员念出来的那一段，远在它进入课堂之前。

intro.en: Lesson travelled from a Latin verb for reading through Old French, and it still carries the sound of a text being read out.
intro.cn: lesson 从一个意为「读」的拉丁动词出发，经古法语传来，至今仍带着「把文本念出来」的意味。

items.en: The verb legere meant to gather, to pick out and then to read, since reading is picking letters out of a page.
items.cn: 动词 legere 意为收集、挑出，进而表示阅读，因为阅读就是从纸面上把字母一个个挑出来。

items.en: The noun lectio named the act of reading and the passage read, and it is the direct source of the word.
items.cn: 名词 lectio 指阅读这个动作，也指被读的那段文字，是本词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French turned lectio into lecon, meaning both a reading and the instruction that came with it.
items.cn: 古法语把 lectio 变成 lecon，同时表示「一段读物」和随之而来的讲授。

items.en: Middle English lesson kept the double sense of a passage read in church and a piece of teaching given to a pupil.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lesson 保留了双重含义：教堂里朗读的一段经文，以及给学生的一次讲授。

items.en: Modern English keeps the church reading as a technical use, while the classroom and moral senses have become the everyday ones.
items.cn: 现代英语把教堂选读保留为专门用法，而课堂与道德训诫的义项成了日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem for reading and the words built on it; the near-meaning group gathers the things a lesson can be.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「读」的拉丁词干及其派生词展开；近义组收 lesson 可以指的那些事物。

entries.definition: A reading or a version of a text, used in church and in scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 诵读；校勘中的文本异文，用于教会与学术场合。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to teach an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为教学而作的正式演讲；讲座。

entries.definition: A story handed down, originally something that was meant to be read.
entries.definitionCN: 流传下来的故事，原指「供阅读的文字」。

entries.definition: Clear enough to be read.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚、可以辨认阅读的。

entries.definition: A period of teaching or the group being taught in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一节课程，或该节课上的一组学生。

entries.definition: A formal teaching talk, usually to many listeners.
entries.definitionCN: 面向众多听众的正式教学演讲。

entries.definition: A small teaching session, often one student or a few.
entries.definitionCN: 小组或个别辅导课。

entries.definition: A whole series of lessons on one subject.
entries.definitionCN: 一门科目的整套课程。

normalIntro.en: The word began as something read aloud and grew into everything a reading can teach, so the hooks follow that path from church to classroom to life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「被朗读的一段」起步，长成阅读所能教的一切，因此记忆钩子沿着从教堂到课堂再到生活的路径展开。

normal.en: Lesson comes from Latin lectio, the act of reading, so a lesson is first of all something that gets read out.
normal.cn: lesson 来自拉丁语 lectio（阅读），所以 lesson 首先是被人念出来的东西。

normal.en: Lecture and lesson share the same Latin stem, which is why a lecture can feel like a lesson for a large room.
normal.cn: lecture 与 lesson 共用同一个拉丁词干，所以讲座也可以像一屋子人共用的一课。

normal.en: Legend, legible and lection all belong to that reading family: what can be read, what is read, what is worth reading.
normal.cn: legend、legible、lection 都属于这个「读」的家族：能读的、被读的、值得读的。

normal.en: The church still keeps the old sense, so a service lists a first lesson and a second lesson rather than readings.
normal.cn: 教堂仍保留古义，所以礼拜程序里写的是第一段选读、第二段选读，而不是普通的朗读。

normal.en: Lesson plan is simply lesson plus plan: the paper that arranges what the class will read and do.
normal.cn: lesson plan 就是 lesson 加 plan：安排课上读什么、做什么的那张纸。

abstract.en: Anything read aloud in a room full of people can turn into something taught, and then into something lived.
abstract.cn: 任何在一屋子人面前被念出来的文字，都能变成被教的东西，再变成被生活验证的东西。

abstract.en: A lesson is a small packet of time with a single point, which is why the word fits a chapter, a class and a warning alike.
abstract.cn: lesson 是一小段只装一个要点的时间，所以它既能指一章书、一节课，也能指一句警告。

abstract.en: The oldest use is still the plainest: someone reads, others listen, and something is passed on.
abstract.cn: 最古老的用法仍然最朴素：有人读，有人听，于是有东西被传下去。

examples.en: The teacher gave us a lesson on plants.
examples.cn: 老师给我们上了一堂关于植物的课。

examples.en: He learned a lesson from that mistake.
examples.cn: 他从那个错误里吸取了教训。

examples.en: The reading of the lesson followed the hymn.
examples.cn: 赞美诗之后是圣经选读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来生」——这辈子上不完的课，下辈子还得接着学；lesson 是课。

root: 拉丁语 legere（收集、挑出、阅读）→ 名词 lectio（阅读；读物）→ 古法语 lecon → 中古英语 lesson；同族词多与「读、讲」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a passage read aloud; from there the word names the time spent on it, the chapter that holds it, the moral it leaves, the rebuke that drives it home, and the church reading itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被朗读的一段」；由此依次指花在它上面的课时、收录它的章节、它留下的道理、把道理打进去的惩戒，以及教堂里的那段选读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher at the blackboard copying out a passage while students bend over their notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板前的老师把一段文字抄下来，学生低头记笔记。

branches.en: a bell ringing at eight for the first class
branches.cn: 八点钟为第一节课敲响的铃声

branches.en: a chapter ending with questions to answer
branches.cn: 以练习提问收尾的一章

branches.en: mud left behind by a flood
branches.cn: 洪水退去后留下的淤泥

branches.en: extra laps run in the rain
branches.cn: 雨里多跑的那几圈

branches.en: a lectern with an open Bible
branches.cn: 放着摊开圣经的读经台

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of reading and its noun, filtered through French, then rebuilt in English with compounds and suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示阅读的拉丁动词及其名词，经过法语过滤，再在英语里用复合词与后缀重新搭建。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 实物教学；可引以为戒的例子

definition_zh: 让；允许；放出；出租；任其（用于祈使或假设）
definition_en: to allow something to happen or someone to do something, to release what is held, to rent out property, and to introduce a wish or command
core_image: 握紧的手松开，牵着的绳子落到地上，被拴住的东西自己走开
scene: 院子里的男人蹲下来解开项圈上的扣，狗在原地抖了抖毛，然后顺着敞开的木门跑进草地。He opened the gate and let the dog run into the field.
sceneCN: 这里是「放开、让……出去」（第 3 个义项：松开并放出被拴住的东西）；句意为男子打开门，让狗跑进草地。图中可辨识物件：项圈、落地的绳子、敞开的木门。

derivatives.zh: 由动词短语 let down 转化而来的名词，义为「失望；令人失望的事」
由 let up 转化而来的名词，义为「停顿；缓和」，多用于否定句
由 out 与 let 复合而成，义为「出口；销路」，指让东西出去的地方
由 let 与 alone 构成的固定短语，义为「更不用说」，用于否定句后追加理由

senses.title: To allow something to happen
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to do something or to be in a certain state
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人做某事，或允许某物处于某种状态
senses.example: Let me carry that box for you.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你搬那个箱子。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to allow to remain and to leave alone, so the core act is stepping back and not stopping what happens next.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的动词意为「任其留着、不去打扰」，所以核心动作是退后一步，不去阻止接下来发生的事。

senses.title: To rent out a room or property
senses.definition: to grant the use of a house or room in return for rent
senses.definitionCN: 把房屋或房间交给别人使用以换取租金
senses.example: The landlord lets the flat by the month.
senses.exampleCN: 房东按月出租这套公寓。
senses.why: Renting out a place is letting it go into someone else's hands for a while, so the same permission verb comes to name a commercial arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把房子租出去，就是让它暂时落到别人手里，于是这个表示「允许」的动词也用来了指一桩买卖安排。

senses.title: To release what is held or contained
senses.definition: to release something that is held, tied or contained so that it can move away
senses.definitionCN: 松开被握住、拴住或装住的东西，让它能够离开
senses.example: She let out a long breath and sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 她长长地吐了口气，坐了下来。
senses.why: If permission is the loosening of a hold, then the physical loosening of a rope, a collar or air under pressure is the same gesture made with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 如果「允许」就是把手上的钳制放松，那么松开绳子、项圈或放出受压的空气，就是用双手做出的同一个动作。

senses.title: Used to express a wish, a command or a supposition
senses.titleCN: 让……吧（用于祈使、意愿或假设）
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to introduce a wish, an order or an assumed case
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句开头，引出愿望、命令或假定情形
senses.example: Let there be light, and the dark room was suddenly clear.
senses.exampleCN: 要有光，昏暗的屋子忽然亮了起来。
senses.why: Once let means to permit, a speaker can permit something into existence by words alone, which is how the verb becomes a way of voicing a wish or a decree.
senses.whyCN: 既然 let 表示允许，说话人便能只用一句话就允许某事物存在，这个词因而成了表达愿望或命令的方式。

senses.title: A property that is rented out
senses.definition: a house or flat that is offered for rent, chiefly in British use
senses.definitionCN: 供出租的房屋或公寓，主要用于英式英语
senses.example: The agent listed the let at a fair rent.
senses.exampleCN: 中介把这套出租房以合理的租金挂了出去。
senses.why: In British usage the action of letting a property is turned back into a noun, so a let is simply the thing that has been let to a tenant.
senses.whyCN: 在英式用法里，把房屋 let 出去这个动作又变回名词，所以 a let 就是那套已经被租给住户的房子。

intro.en: Let is a plain Germanic verb that has never needed a prefix; its history is a history of loosening a hold.
intro.cn: let 是一个朴素的日耳曼语动词，从不需要前缀；它的历史就是「松开一道钳制」的历史。

items.en: A root reconstructed as lē- is generally thought to mean to let go or to be slack, and from it both the Germanic verb and words for slowness are traced.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 lē-，意为「放开、松弛」，日耳曼语动词与表示「迟缓」的词都被追溯到它。

items.en: The strong verb lǣtan meant to allow, to leave behind and to let go, and it formed its past tense as lēt.
items.cn: 古英语强动词 lǣtan 意为允许、留下、放开，过去式作 lēt。

items.en: Middle English leten levelled the past tense to let, so that the present and the past fell together in spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语的 leten 把过去式拉平为 let，于是现在式与过去式在拼写上合而为一。

items.en: By this period let was also used at the head of clauses to express a wish or command, as in let there be and let us pray.
items.cn: 到这一时期，let 也开始放在从句开头表达愿望或命令，如 let there be、let us pray。

items.en: Modern English adds the commercial sense of renting out property and the British noun a let, while keeping fixed phrases such as let alone and let go.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「出租房屋」的商业义项和英式名词 a let，同时保留 let alone、let go 等固定短语。

normal.en: Let is one of the verbs that refuse to change in the past: today I let, yesterday I let.
normal.cn: let 属于过去式不变的那类动词：今天 let，昨天也 let。

normal.en: The present participle doubles the final consonant, so it is letting, not leting.
normal.cn: 现在分词要双写词尾辅音，所以是 letting，不是 leting。

normal.en: Let go and let out are the two oldest gestures of the word: release a hold, release what is inside.
normal.cn: let go 与 let out 是这个词最古老的两个动作：松开钳制，放出里面的东西。

normal.en: To let a flat is to permit its use for payment, which is why British signs say flat to let.
normal.cn: to let a flat 就是允许别人付费使用它，所以英式招租牌上写 flat to let。

normal.en: Let alone follows a negative clause and adds something even less likely, as in he cannot walk, let alone run.
normal.cn: let alone 跟在否定从句后面，再补上更不可能的事，如他走都走不了，更别说跑。

abstract.en: Every sense of let is the same loosening, seen at a hand, a door and a contract.
abstract.cn: let 的每个义项都是同一次松手，只是分别发生在手上、门上和一纸租约上。

abstract.en: A word that permits can also create: once you may allow a thing to be, saying so is enough.
abstract.cn: 一个表示允许的词也能创造：既然你可以允许某物存在，说出来就够了。

abstract.en: Hands open, dog runs, room is rented: permission is always a small release of control.
abstract.cn: 手一松，狗就跑，屋子也租了出去：允许从来都是把控制松开一点。

senses.title: The height of something above the ground
senses.definition: the height of a surface or mass, measured from the ground or from a fixed line
senses.definitionCN: 某表面或物体相对地面，或相对某条固定基准线的高度
senses.example: The water level had dropped to the children's knees.
senses.exampleCN: 水位已经降到孩子们的膝盖那么低。
senses.why: The Latin libella was a plumb line and a small water tube used on building sites; measuring upward from a trusted flat line is exactly the job of that instrument, so the first sense is a measured height.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 libella 是铅垂线和小水器，在工地上专门用来从一条可信的平线往上量；所以这个词最早的义项就是量出来的高度。

senses.title: A standard or amount used for comparison
senses.definition: the amount, rank or quality of something, especially when set beside other things
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的数量、等级或质量，尤指与其他事物并排比较时
senses.example: Her reading level is far above her age.
senses.exampleCN: 她的阅读水平远远超过她的年龄。
senses.why: Once a flat line is trusted, it can serve as a reference for anything else; the word then leaves space and becomes a scale on which people and results are placed.
senses.whyCN: 一条平线一旦可信，就能当作其他东西的参照；于是这个词离开空间，变成一把给人或成果定位的尺子。

senses.title: One floor of a building
senses.definition: one of the floors or storeys of a building, counted upward from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物中的一层，从地面往上计数
senses.example: The library takes up the third level of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆占了这栋楼的第三层。
senses.why: A tall building is a stack of flat horizontal slices, and every slice rests at one height; English names that slice with the same word it uses for the height itself.
senses.whyCN: 高楼是一层层水平切片叠起来的，每一片都停在一个高度；英语就用表示「高度」的同一个词来命名这一片。

senses.title: Flat and even, with no part higher than another
senses.definition: having a surface that is flat and even, with no part standing above the rest
senses.definitionCN: 表面平直，没有一处高过其余部分
senses.example: The floor must be level before the tiles go down.
senses.exampleCN: 铺地砖之前地面必须是平的。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the literal picture: the surface a plumb line or a water tube would approve of, with nothing sticking up anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留最字面的画面：那是铅垂线或水管量过也挑不出毛病、任何地方都没有突起的面。

senses.title: To make a surface flat or knock a building down
senses.definition: to make something flat and even, or to bring a building down until it meets the ground
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弄平，或把建筑物拆到与地面齐平
senses.example: Workers levelled the old wall to make room for the park.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把旧墙推平，为公园腾出地方。
senses.why: If evenness is the goal, the verb is the labour of reaching it; tearing a building down leaves the ground at a single height, so demolition joins the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然「平」是要达到的状态，动词就是达到它的那番劳作；把楼拆掉之后地面只剩一个高度，于是拆除也归进同一个词。

intro.en: Level comes from a Latin word for a balance, shrunk into the name of a small measuring instrument, then reshaped by French before English widened it.
intro.cn: level 来自拉丁语中表示「天平」的词，先缩成一件小测量器具的名字，又经法语改写，最后被英语大幅扩展。

items.en: Libra meant a balance or a pair of scales, and it also named a Roman unit of weight.
items.cn: libra 意为天平、秤，同时也指罗马的一种重量单位。

items.en: A libella was a small balance; on a building site it meant a plumb line or a little water tube for testing whether a surface was even.
items.cn: libella 是小天平；在工地上它指铅垂线或测平的小水器，用来检验一个面是否平直。

items.en: Old French kept the word as livel, still tied to the instrument and to the idea of an even surface.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 livel，仍与那件器具以及「表面平直」的观念相连。

items.en: Middle English level first names the instrument for testing flatness, then the flat surface itself.
items.cn: 中古英语的 level 先指检验平直的器具，随后指平直的面本身。

items.en: Modern English extends level to height above the ground, standards of achievement, floors of buildings, and the act of flattening.
items.cn: 现代英语把 level 扩展到离地高度、成就水平、楼房层数，以及弄平的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of weighing and balancing; the near-meaning group gathers words for height, rank and flatness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「称量、平衡」的词干展开；近义组收表示高度、等级与平坦的词。

entries.definition: A balance or pair of scales in Latin, and the name of the zodiac sign of the scales.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的天平或秤，也是黄道十二宫天秤座的名字。

entries.definition: The small balance that became the plumb line and water level of builders.
entries.definitionCN: 由「天平」缩成的小词，后来成为工匠的铅垂线与水平器。

entries.definition: A state of balance, built on the Latin word for a pair of scales.
entries.definitionCN: 平衡状态，建立在拉丁语「天平」一词之上。

entries.definition: Carefully weighed in the mind, from a Latin verb meaning to weigh.
entries.definitionCN: 经过仔细权衡的，来自意为「称量」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The distance from the ground upward.
entries.definitionCN: 从地面往上的距离；高度。

entries.definition: A level of quality used as a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 用作衡量标准的质量水准。

entries.definition: A floor of a building, the usual British word.
entries.definitionCN: 楼房的层，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: Smooth and even, with no bumps or slopes.
entries.definitionCN: 平滑而没有突起或倾斜的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a little balance used to test a flat surface, and its family keeps returning to evenness and measurement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一件用来检验平面小天平，同族词反复回到「平」与「量」。

normal.en: Libra is Latin for a balance, and libella is its small form, so level starts life as a tool for judging whether a surface is even.
normal.cn: libra 是拉丁语的「天平」，libella 是它的小称，所以 level 最初是一件判断表面平不平的工具。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs straight down, and a surface is level when that line meets it squarely.
normal.cn: 铅垂线笔直垂下，当一个面与它正好垂直相交时，那个面就是平的。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l: levelled and levelling; American spelling keeps one l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 levelled 与 levelling；美式只写一个 l。

normal.en: Sea level is the even reference line from which heights on land are measured.
normal.cn: 海平面就是那条水平的基准线，陆地上的高度都从它量起。

normal.en: To level a building is to take away every height that stood above the ground.
normal.cn: 把一栋楼 level 掉，就是把高过地面的每一寸都去掉。

abstract.en: One word covering height, rank, floor and flattening suggests English sees them all as positions on a single even line.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示高度、等级、楼层和弄平，说明英语把它们都看成同一条平线上的位置。

abstract.en: Fairness borrows the same picture: a level playing field gives nobody a slope to run down.
abstract.cn: 公平也借用了同一幅画面：平坦的球场不会给任何人一个下坡。

abstract.en: Checking a surface with a bubble is a small act of trusting gravity to tell the truth.
abstract.cn: 用气泡检验一个面，是让重力说真话的一件小事。

examples.en: The water level had dropped to the children's knees.
examples.cn: 水位已经降到孩子们的膝盖那么低。

examples.en: The floor must be level before the tiles go down.
examples.cn: 铺地砖之前地面必须是平的。

examples.en: Workers levelled the old wall to make room for the park.
examples.cn: 工人们把旧墙推平，为公园腾出地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来我这儿」——干活前先看看地面平不平；level 就是水平、弄平。

root: 拉丁语 libra（天平、秤）的指小形式 libella（小天平、铅垂线），经古法语 livel 进入英语；同族词多与称量、平直有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line that sits even with the ground; from it flow measured height, rank on a scale, stacked floors, and the adjective and verb of flatness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条与地面齐平的线；由此分出量出的高度、尺度上的等级、叠起的楼层，以及表示「平」的形容词和动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bubble resting between two marks in a glass tube laid across a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃管横放在木板上，管里的气泡停在两道刻线之间。

branches.en: a river gauge recording how high the water stands
branches.cn: 记录水位高低的河尺

branches.en: a bubble settling in the middle of a tube
branches.cn: 气泡停在管子中央

branches.en: a chart ranking readers by reading age
branches.cn: 按阅读年龄给读者分级的图表

branches.en: a lift stopping at a numbered floor
branches.cn: 停在某一层的电梯

branches.en: a wall coming down until the ground is clear
branches.cn: 墙被推倒，直到地面清空

intro.en: A Latin balance, its small form, a French reshaping and two English suffixes carry this word from instrument to height, rank and floor.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「天平」、它的指小形式、一次法语改写和两个英语后缀，把这个词从器具一路带到高度、等级与楼层。

latinIntro.en: Libra and its small form libella belong to the Latin vocabulary of weighing and measuring, and both are recorded words.
latinIntro.cn: libra 与它的指小形式 libella 都属于拉丁语称量与测量的词汇，两者都是有记录的实词。

a small balance, a plumb line

items.meaningCN: 把东西弄平的人；平等主义者
