definition_zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文学科的
definition_en: open to different views, favouring political reform, generous in amount, not strict or literal, or relating to a broad education in the arts and sciences
core_image: 一个不被绳索束缚的人，伸手把东西分给别人
scene: 社区听证会上，一位议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房。The liberal member spoke for more low-income housing and argued that the planning rules should be looser.
sceneCN: 这里 liberal 是「政治立场偏自由派、支持改革的」（第 2 个义项：政治上的自由主义）；句意：这位自由派议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房，并主张规划规则应当更宽松。图中可辨识物件：听证会标牌、麦克风、住房规划图、选民登记表。

pos.zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文教育的
自由主义者；自由派支持者

derivatives.zh: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地
自由主义
使自由化；放宽限制
不宽容的；反自由的

senses.title: Open to different views
senses.titleCN: 开明的：能容纳不同意见
senses.definition: willing to accept and tolerate behaviour or opinions different from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受并容忍与自己不同的行为或观点
senses.example: Her parents were liberal about curfews, as long as she called home.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母对宵禁时间很开明，只要她打电话回家就行。
senses.why: The core is Latin liber 'free'. A liberal mind is not bound by a narrow rule or prejudice; it leaves room for what it did not expect.
senses.whyCN: 核心是拉丁语 liber“自由的”。开明的头脑不被狭窄的规矩或偏见捆住，会为意料之外的东西留出空间。

senses.title: Politically reform-minded
senses.definition: favouring social reform, individual rights and government action, often associated with the centre-left
senses.definitionCN: 支持社会改革、个人权利与政府作为，常与中左政治立场相关
senses.example: The liberal party lost its rural seats in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 自由派政党在选举中失去了乡村选区。
senses.why: In 19c politics liberal meant free from arbitrary rule and favouring constitutional government. The label later shifted toward social reform, and its meaning still varies by country.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪政治中，liberal 指免于专断统治、支持宪政。这个标签后来偏向社会改革，其含义至今因国家而异。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.definition: given or existing in large amounts; more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 给予或存在的量大；足够而有余
senses.example: Add a liberal amount of olive oil before roasting.
senses.exampleCN: 烤之前加足量的橄榄油。
senses.why: Latin liberalis already meant 'generous, munificent'. The free man was expected to give freely, so the adjective moved from social status to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liberalis 本就有“慷慨、大方”之义。自由人被认为应当大方给予，于是形容词从社会身份滑到了数量。

senses.title: Not strictly literal
senses.definition: not strictly literal or exact; allowing freedom in interpretation or wording
senses.definitionCN: 不严格依照字面或精确表述；在解释或措辞上留出自由
senses.example: The translator took a liberal reading of the poem's last line.
senses.exampleCN: 译者对诗的最后一行作了较自由的解读。
senses.why: Freedom applies to wording: a liberal translation or interpretation departs from the letter in order to keep the sense.
senses.whyCN: 自由落在措辞上：liberal translation 或 interpretation 离开字面，为的是保住意思。

senses.title: Of a broad education in the arts
senses.titleCN: 博雅教育的：人文学科的
senses.definition: relating to a broad education in humanities, social sciences and sciences rather than narrow technical training
senses.definitionCN: 与人文、社会科学和自然科学的广博教育有关，而非狭窄的技术训练
senses.example: He studied liberal arts before law school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法学院之前读的是人文学科。
senses.why: artes liberales were the skills befitting a free citizen, as opposed to a slave or a tradesman. Liberal arts still names that ideal of a broad, non-vocational education.
senses.whyCN: artes liberales 是“配得上自由公民的技艺”，区别于奴隶或工匠的技能。liberal arts 至今指这种广博而非职业化的教育理想。

senses.title: Noun: a person of liberal views
senses.definition: a person who holds liberal political or social views
senses.definitionCN: 持自由派政治或社会观点的人
senses.example: The bill split the liberals in the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项议案让参议院里的自由派分裂了。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun by metonymy: a person is named by the position they hold. Politics is the usual setting for this use.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过转喻变成可数名词：用一个人所持的立场来指这个人。这种用法通常出现在政治语境。

senses.title: Free-market economics
senses.titleCN: 经济上的自由市场主张
senses.definition: favouring free markets, private ownership and little state control, in the classical economic sense
senses.definitionCN: 在古典经济学意义上支持自由市场、私有制与较少的国家控制
senses.example: The party is liberal on trade but cautious on welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在贸易上主张自由，在福利上却谨慎。
senses.why: Classical liberalism put economic freedom alongside political freedom. Note the trap: in US politics 'liberal' often means the opposite on economic policy, so the sense depends on context.
senses.whyCN: 古典自由主义把经济自由与政治自由并列。注意陷阱：在美国政治语境中，liberal 在经济政策上常指相反方向，因此词义要看上下文。

senses.title: Liberal with: giving freely
senses.definition: generous in giving something to other people, sometimes to the point of excess
senses.definitionCN: 在给予他人某物时很大方，有时到了过分的程度
senses.example: He was liberal with praise and stingy with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸人毫不吝啬，给细节却很小气。
senses.why: Here the quantity sense is directed at people. Liberal with praise means the giving hand opens wide; the same phrase can quietly criticize someone who gives too freely.
senses.whyCN: 这里数量义对准了人。liberal with praise 意味着给予的手张得很开；同一短语也可以暗含批评，指某人给得过头。

senses.title: Not strict: allowing latitude
senses.definition: not strictly enforced or tightly controlled; allowing freedom of action
senses.definitionCN: 不被严格执行或 tightly 控制；允许行动自由
senses.example: The school has a liberal policy on mobile phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校对手机的规定很宽松。
senses.why: The freedom is now built into an arrangement, not into a person's mind. A liberal policy leaves the margin wide, which is why the word can describe rules as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 这时自由被写进了安排本身，而不是某人的头脑。宽松的政策把余地留得很宽，因此这个词既能形容人，也能形容规则。

intro.en: Liberal comes from Latin liber 'free', not from liber 'book'. Its oldest English sense was 'generous, noble', and 'free' ran through both the social and the educational branches.
intro.cn: liberal 出自拉丁语 liber“自由的”，不是 liber“书”。它最早的英语义是“慷慨、高贵”，而“自由”贯穿了社会与教育这两条分支。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'generous, noble, free', especially of a person of high birth or a free citizen.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪中期的英语，意为“慷慨的、高贵的、自由的”，尤指出身高贵者或自由公民。

items.en: liberalis 'of a free person, noble, generous, munificent' is formed from liber 'free' plus -alis.
items.cn: liberalis“属于自由人的、高贵的、慷慨的”由 liber“自由的”加 -alis 构成。

items.en: liber 'free' and liber 'book' are two different nouns. Library comes from librarium 'bookcase', built on liber 'book / inner bark', so library is not a relative of liberal.
items.cn: liber“自由的”与 liber“书”是两个不同的名词。library 出自 librarium“书柜”，建在 liber“书／树内皮”上，因此 library 不是 liberal 的亲戚。

items.en: artes liberales were 'the arts befitting a free person', the broad curriculum of grammar, rhetoric, logic, arithmetic, geometry, music and astronomy. English liberal arts is a calque of that phrase.
items.cn: artes liberales 是“配得上自由人的技艺”，包括语法、修辞、逻辑、算术、几何、音乐与天文这一广博课程。英语 liberal arts 就是该短语的仿译。

items.en: liber is connected with PIE *leudh- 'free, grow' (some sources gloss it 'people'). This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: liber 与原始印欧语 *leudh-“自由、成长”相联系（也有资料解作“人民”）。这一重构属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: The political sense develops in the 19c around constitutional government and free trade. In 20c US English liberal came to mean social reform and state action, which is why the word can sound opposite in different countries. It is never related to licere 'be permitted' (license).
items.cn: 政治义在 19 世纪围绕宪政与自由贸易发展起来。到 20 世纪美国英语中，liberal 转指社会改革与国家作为，因此这个词在不同国家听起来可能相反。它与 licere“被允许”（license）从无关系。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the two different Latins: liber 'free' gives liberty, liberate and liberal, while liber 'book' gives library. The near-meaning group separates the political label from attitude and amount words.
note.cn: 形近组的关键是两个不同的拉丁词：liber“自由的”给出 liberty、liberate、liberal，而 liber“书”给出 library。近义组把政治标签与态度词、数量词分开。

entries.definition: freedom from control or restriction. It is the abstract noun of liber 'free', the same source as liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 免于控制或限制的自由。它是 liber“自由的”的抽象名词，与 liberal 同源。

entries.definition: to set someone free from control, prison or occupation. It is the verb from liberare, the same 'free' family.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人摆脱控制、监禁或占领。它出自 liberare，属于同一个“自由”词族。

entries.definition: a place where books are kept. It looks like liberal, but it comes from liber 'book / inner bark' through librarium, not from liber 'free'.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书的地方。它形似 liberal，却出自 liber“书／树内皮”经 librarium 演变，不是 liber“自由的”。

entries.definition: favouring reform or new ideas, often more activist than liberal. It is a political label, not a word for generosity or education.
entries.definitionCN: 支持改革或新观念的，通常比 liberal 更行动派。它是政治标签，不表示慷慨或教育。

entries.definition: willing to accept differences. It names the attitude itself and carries no political programme.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异的。它只指态度本身，不携带政治纲领。

entries.definition: giving much or containing much. It overlaps liberal in amount and giving, but has no political or educational sense.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很多或含量充足的。它在数量与给予义上与 liberal 重叠，但没有政治或教育义。

entries.definition: willing to consider new ideas. It is more personal and less ideological than liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意考虑新观念的。它比 liberal 更个人化，意识形态色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: liber 'free' + -alis, with liberty, liberate and deliver in the same family. The look-alike library belongs to liber 'book' and must be kept apart.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：liber“自由的”+ -alis，同族有 liberty、liberate、deliver。形近的 library 属于 liber“书”，必须分开。

normal.en: liber 'free' is the stem: liberal, liberty, liberate and deliver all carry some form of 'freeing'.
normal.cn: liber“自由的”是词干：liberal、liberty、liberate、deliver 都带有某种“使自由”的意思。

normal.en: artes liberales were the skills of a free citizen, which is why liberal arts means a broad education rather than a political opinion.
normal.cn: artes liberales 是自由公民的技艺，所以 liberal arts 指广博教育，而不是政治观点。

normal.en: library comes from liber 'book', a different noun. A library is a book-place, not a freedom-place.
normal.cn: library 出自另一个名词 liber“书”。图书馆是放书的地方，不是放自由的地方。

normal.en: deliver is de- 'away' + liberare 'free': to deliver a parcel is to free it from your hands into someone else's.
normal.cn: deliver 是 de-“离开”+ liberare“使自由”：把包裹交付出去，就是让它离开你的手、到别人手里。

normal.en: liberal with praise uses the generosity branch, not the political one: the hand gives freely.
normal.cn: liberal with praise 走的是“慷慨”分支，不是政治分支：手在大方地给。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with no lock: a person can walk out, and because they can walk out, they can also leave room for others to walk in. Liberal is that unlocked gate, applied to minds, rules and money.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门：人能走出去，也正因为能走出去，才会给别人留出走进来的余地。liberal 就是这扇没锁的门，用在头脑、规则与金钱上。

abstract.en: Freedom can be spent in three directions: given away as generosity, kept open as tolerance, or written into a curriculum as the education of a free person.
abstract.cn: 自由可以花在三个方向：作为慷慨被给出去，作为宽容被留开，或作为自由人的教育被写进课程。

abstract.en: The same word can mean 'leave it loose' and 'give a lot'. Both are the image of a hand that does not close.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以指“放宽”，也可以指“给得多”。两者都是同一幅图：一只不握紧的手。

examples.en: A liberal education taught her to question her own assumptions.
examples.cn: 博雅教育教会她质疑自己的预设。

examples.en: Pour a liberal amount of sauce over the fish.
examples.cn: 在鱼上浇足量的酱汁。

examples.en: He is socially liberal but fiscally conservative.
examples.cn: 他在社会议题上开明，在财政上保守。

dict_mnemonic.text: “离不了”——离不了自由，凡事主张放开 → liberal 自由的、开明的

root: 拉丁语 liber“自由的”（不是 liber“书”）+ -alis，核心是“不受束缚的、像自由人那样给予”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of liberal, all variations on 'not bound': a mind not bound by prejudice, a politics of reform, a hand that gives widely, a reading not bound to the letter, an education for a free person, and rules left loose.
sensesIntro.cn: liberal 的九个义项都是“不受束缚”的变体：不被偏见捆住的头脑、改革的政治、给得宽的手、不囿于字面的解读、自由人的教育，以及留得很松的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbound person, whose hand is free to give and whose mind is free to admit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被捆住的人，手可以自由给予，头脑可以自由接纳。

branches.en: OPEN AND LOOSE: the same freedom applied to a mind and to a set of rules.
branches.cn: 开明与宽松：同一种自由，用在头脑上，也用在规则上。

branches.en: POLITICS AND ECONOMY: the reform label, the person who wears it, and the free-market branch.
branches.cn: 政治与经济：改革标签、持标签的人，以及自由市场分支。

branches.en: GENEROSITY: abundance in amount, and the open hand that gives to people.
branches.cn: 慷慨：数量上的充足，以及向人张开的手。

branches.en: INTERPRETATION: freedom from the literal letter in reading and translation.
branches.cn: 解释：在阅读与翻译中摆脱字面的束缚。

branches.en: EDUCATION: artes liberales, the broad curriculum of a free person.
branches.cn: 教育：artes liberales，自由人的广博课程。

intro.en: Liberal takes ordinary English suffixes: -ly for the adverb, -ism for the system, -ize for the verb, and il- as a negative prefix before l.
intro.cn: liberal 接的是普通英语后缀：-ly 构成副词，-ism 构成主义，-ize 构成动词，il- 则在 l 前作否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of liber 'free' includes liberty, liberate, deliver and libertine. Library belongs to the other liber, 'book', and is not part of this family.
latinIntro.cn: liber“自由的”这一拉丁词族包括 liberty、liberate、deliver、libertine。library 属于另一个 liber“书”，不在这个词族里。

items.meaning: generously, in large amounts, or in an open-minded way
items.meaningCN: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apply the cream liberally to the burned area.
items.exampleCN: 在烫伤处大量涂抹药膏。

items.meaning: the political and economic doctrine of liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 自由主义（-ism 构成主义、学说）
items.exampleCN: 古典自由主义支持自由贸易。

items.meaning: to make rules or systems less strict
items.meaningCN: 使自由化；放宽（-ize 表示“使……”）
items.example: The government liberalized the visa rules.

items.meaning: not tolerant of different views; opposed to liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 不宽容的；反自由的（il- 是否定前缀）
items.example: The ban was criticized as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项禁令被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The adjective sits at the centre of liberal and liberty.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 liberal 与 liberty 的共同核心。

items.example: It carries the free adjective into English as liberal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“自由”这个形容词带进英语成为 liberal。

items.structure: suffix naming a system or movement
items.meaning: a body of doctrine or practice
items.example: It forms liberalism, the political doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberalism 这一政治学说。

items.example: It forms liberality, the quality of being generous or open.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberality，即慷慨或开明的品质。

items.example: The army liberated the city at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时解放了这座城市。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 自由；免于控制（-tas 构成抽象名词，经法语入英语）

latinEntries.meaning: to set someone or something free
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解放；使自由（出自 liberare“使自由”）

latinEntries.meaning: to hand over, save, or set free; literally 'to free away'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 交付；解救；字面“使脱离而自由”（de- + liberare）

latinEntries.meaning: a person without moral restraint; originally a freed slave
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡者；原指被释放的奴隶（自由义走偏为“无约束”）
